Hissa 01 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Getting Started

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Getting Started. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Getting Started — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: ye poore Getting Started track ka landing page hai. Ye Next.js App Router ko "full-stack web applications" banane ke tareeke ke roop me pesh karta hai. Ye woh prerequisite knowledge batata hai jo docs maan kar chalte hain: HTML, CSS, JavaScript aur React. Jo log naye hain, unhe shuru karne se pehle React Foundations course aur Next.js Foundations course (jisme ek dashboard app banta hai) ki taraf bheja jata hai.

Isme kya list hai (track ka order — yahi is SPA ke Part 1 ki reedh hai): Installation → Project Structure → Layouts and Pages → Linking and Navigating → Server and Client Components → Fetching Data → Mutating Data → Caching → Revalidating → Error Handling → CSS → Image Optimization → Font Optimization → Metadata aur OG images → Route Handlers → Proxy → Deploying → Upgrading.

Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
docs khule taur par App Router ko full-stack ke roop me pesh karte hain (ek hi framework me frontend + backend), sirf ek React renderer ke roop me nahi.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started
Hissa 02 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Installation

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Installation. Ek line me samjho to: create-next-app CLI se naya Next.js application kaise banate hain, aur TypeScript, ESLint aur Module Path Aliases kaise setup karte hain. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Installation — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: System requirements, Supported browsers (zero config), Quick start (all package managers), CLI prompts (customize settings), Good to know. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

System requirements: Node.js 20.9+ minimum; macOS, Windows (WSL samet), Linux. Supported browsers (zero config): Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+.

Quick start (saare package managers):

%
bash
npx create-next-app@latest my-app --yes
cd my-app
npm run dev
# visit http://localhost:3000
%

(pnpm: pnpm create next-app@latest my-app --yes phir pnpm dev; yarn: yarn create next-app@latest my-app --yes; bun: bun create next-app@latest my-app --yes.)

--yes save ki gayi preferences/defaults ka use karke prompts ko skip kar deta hai. Default setup inhe enable karta hai: TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, App Router, Turbopack, import alias @/*, aur coding agents ko guide karne ke liye ek AGENTS.md file.

CLI prompts (settings customize karo): TypeScript? (Yes/No); linter: ESLint / Biome / None; React Compiler?; Tailwind CSS?; src/ directory?; App Router? (recommended); Cache Components?; import alias (@/* default); AGENTS.md shamil karein?

Manual installation (step by step):

%
bash
npm i next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
%

Phir package.json me scripts jodo:

%
json
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev",
    "build": "next build",
    "start": "next start",
    "lint": "eslint",
    "lint:fix": "eslint --fix"
  }
}
%

next dev = Turbopack (default bundler) ke saath dev server; next build = production build; next start = production server. Iske bajay Webpack use karna ho to: next dev --webpack / next build --webpack.

Jaanna achha rahega: App Router built-in React canary releases use karta hai (saare stable React 19 changes plus naye framework-validated features), lekin tooling/ecosystem compatibility ke liye tumhe react aur react-dom ko package.json me phir bhi declare karna hoga. Pages Router package.json wala React version use karta hai.

app directory banao: file-system routing — routes file structure se tay hote hain. app/ banao jisme ek layout.tsx ho (root layout, required — isme <html> aur <body> tags hone chahiye) aur ek app/page.tsx:

%
tsx
// app/layout.tsx
export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
% %
tsx
// app/page.tsx
export default function Page() {
  return <h1>Hello, Next.js!</h1>
}
%

Agar tum root layout bhool jao, to next dev chalane par Next.js use automatic bana deta hai. Project root par optional src/ folder app code ko configuration files se alag rakhta hai.

public folder (optional): static assets (images, fonts). Base URL / se reference hote hain — jaise public/profile.png → /profile.png, next/image ke saath use ke liye:

%
tsx
import Image from 'next/image'
export default function Page() {
  return <Image src="/profile.png" alt="Profile" width={100} height={100} />
}
%

Dev server chalao: npm run dev → http://localhost:3000 par jao → app/page.tsx edit karo, save karo, update dekho (Fast Refresh).

TypeScript setup: minimum TS v5.1.0. Kisi file ka naam .ts/.tsx rakho aur next dev chalao — Next.js deps automatic install karke recommended options ke saath tsconfig.json jod deta hai. IDE plugin: VS Code me Command Palette → "TypeScript: Select TypeScript Version" → "Use Workspace Version", taaki Next.js ka custom TS plugin/type checker use ho.

Editor setup (same-naam wale tabs ki problem): App Router ki files ke naam sab page.tsx, layout.tsx wagera hote hain. VS Code 1.88+ / Cursor me .vscode/settings.json me custom editor labels jodo taaki tabs me enclosing folders dikhein (jaise blog/[id] - page.tsx):

%
json
{
  "workbench.editor.customLabels.patterns": {
    "**/app/**/page.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - page.tsx",
    "**/app/**/layout.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - layout.tsx",
    "**/app/**/loading.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - loading.tsx",
    "**/app/**/error.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - error.tsx",
    "**/app/**/not-found.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - not-found.tsx",
    "**/app/**/template.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - template.tsx",
    "**/app/**/default.tsx": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - default.tsx",
    "**/app/**/route.ts": "${dirname(1)}/${dirname} - route.ts"
  }
}
%

JetBrains IDEs folder automatic dikhate hain — koi setup nahi chahiye.

Linting: ESLint ya Biome. Scripts: "lint": "eslint", "lint:fix": "eslint --fix"; ya Biome "lint": "biome check", "format": "biome format --write". Purane next lint ko npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . se migrate karo. Important (Next.js 16): next build ab linter ko automatic nahi chalata — use npm scripts se chalao. ESLint use kar rahe ho to ek explicit config (recommended eslint.config.mjs) banao.

Absolute imports / module path aliases: tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json me baseUrl + paths configure karo:

%
json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": "src/",
    "paths": {
      "@/styles/*": ["styles/*"],
      "@/components/*": ["components/*"]
    }
  }
}
%

Ye import { Button } from '../../../components/button' ko import { Button } from '@/components/button' me badal deta hai. Paths baseUrl ke relative hote hain.

Upgrading: npx next upgrade (pnpm: pnpm next upgrade; bun: bunx next upgrade). Upgrade karne se next package ke andar node_modules/next/dist/docs/ me bundled docs bhi update ho jate hain, isliye AI coding agents installed version se kaam karte hain, training data se nahi. Agent-driven upgrade: npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest. Preview docs: https://preview.nextjs.org.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Node < 20.9 fail ho jayega — pehle version check karo.
  • Root layout bhool jana auto-fix ho jata hai, lekin auto-generated wala bare hota hai; hamesha <html lang="en"> ke saath apna khud ka likho.
  • Next.js 16 me ye mat samjho ki next build tumhare liye lint chalata hai — ab nahi chalata.
  • package.json me react/react-dom declare na karna tooling tod deta hai, bhale hi App Router React canary bundle karta hai.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
create-next-app manual setup par kyun behtar hai (conventions wired: TS, Tailwind, ESLint, Turbopack, alias, AGENTS.md); Turbopack kya hai (default bundler, --webpack flag se Webpack); root layout me <html>/<body> kyun hona chahiye; @/* alias kya hai aur paths/baseUrl kaise kaam karte hain.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation
Hissa 03 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Project structure and organization

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Project structure and organization. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Project structure and organization — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — top-level folders:

FolderPurpose
appApp Router
pagesPages Router
publicstatic assets, jo / se serve hote hain
srcoptional application source folder

Top-level files: next.config.js (config), package.json (deps + scripts), instrumentation.ts (OpenTelemetry), proxy.ts (request proxy), .env / .env.local / .env.production / .env.development (env vars — kabhi commit mat karo), eslint.config.mjs, .gitignore, next-env.d.ts (TS declarations — track nahi karte), tsconfig.json / jsconfig.json.

Routing files (special file conventions):

FileExtensionsRole
layout.js .jsx .tsxshared UI (header/nav/footer)
page.js .jsx .tsxroute ka UI — yahi file route ko public banati hai
loading.js .jsx .tsxloading UI (Suspense boundary)
not-found.js .jsx .tsxnot-found UI
error.js .jsx .tsxerror UI (error boundary)
global-error.js .jsx .tsxglobal error UI
route.js .tsAPI endpoint
template.js .jsx .tsxdobara render hone wala layout (layout se alag, navigation par remount hota hai)
default.js .jsx .tsxparallel route ka fallback page

Nested routes: har folder ek URL segment hota hai; folders ko nest karne se segments bhi nest ho jate hain; kisi bhi level ka layout apne child segments ko wrap karta hai. Ek route tabhi public hota hai jab usme page ya route file maujud ho. Jaise app/blog/authors/page.tsx → /blog/authors.

Dynamic routes: [segment] single param, [...segment] catch-all, [[...segment]] optional catch-all. Inhe params prop se access karte hain. Udaharan: app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx → /blog/my-first-post; app/shop/[...slug]/page.tsx → /shop/clothing/shirts; app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx → /docs khud bhi.

Route groups aur private folders: (group) URL ko badle bina routes ko organize karta hai — jaise app/(marketing)/page.tsx → /, app/(shop)/cart/page.tsx → /cart; har group ka apna layout bhi ho sakta hai. _folder (private folder) us folder aur uske saare subfolders ko routing se bahar kar deta hai — colocated components/utils rakhne ki safe jagah, jaise app/blog/_components/Post.tsx, app/blog/_lib/data.ts.

Parallel aur intercepting routes: @slot ek named slot hai jo parent layout render karta hai (jaise sidebar + main). Intercepting pattern URL badle bina, maujuda layout ke andar hi dusra route dikha deta hai (list ke upar modal jaisa): (.)folder same level, (..)folder parent level, (..)(..)folder do level upar, (...)folder root se.

Metadata file conventions: favicon (.ico), icon (.ico/.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.svg ya .js/.ts/.tsx se generated), apple-icon (.jpg/.jpeg/.png ya generated), opengraph-image / twitter-image (.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.gif ya generated), sitemap (.xml ya generated .js/.ts), robots (.txt ya generated).

Component hierarchy (render order): layout.js → template.js → error.js (error boundary) → loading.js (Suspense boundary) → not-found.js → page.js ya nested layout.js. Components recursively render hote hain — ek segment ke components apne parent ke andar nest hote hain.

Colocation: route structure folders se banti hai, lekin ek route tab tak publicly accessible nahi hota jab tak usme page.js ya route.js na joda jaye; aur client ko sirf wahi content bheja jata hai jo page.js/route.js return karta hai. Isliye project files ko route segments ke andar safe tareeke se colocate kiya ja sakta hai — wo routable nahi banti. Private folders (_folder) colocation ke liye zaroori nahi hain, lekin madad karte hain: UI ko routing logic se alag rakhna, consistent organization, aur future Next.js conventions ke saath naming conflicts se bachna. Tip: underscore se shuru hone wala URL segment %5FfolderName likha jata hai.

src folder: optional hai; app code (jisme app bhi hai) isme rakha jata hai taaki wo root ki config files se alag rahe.

Organization strategies (Next.js unopinionated hai — ek chuno, consistent raho):

1. Project files app ke bahar: shared components/lib project root par; app sirf routing ke liye. 2. app ke andar top-level folders: shared code app ki root me. 3. Feature/route ke hisaab se split: globally shared code app root par; specific code unhi route segments me colocate karo jo use use karte hain. 4. URL par asar dale bina organize karne ke liye route groups: (marketing) banam (shop), har ek ka apna layout, app layout ke neeche nested. 5. Sirf kuch segments ko layout me opt-in karna: sirf un routes ko group me rakho jo layout share karte hain (jaise account + cart ke saath (shop); checkout bahar rehta hai). 6. Loading skeleton sirf ek route par: loading.tsx ko /(overview) jaise route group ke andar rakho taaki wo sirf dashboard → overview par lagu ho. 7. Multiple root layouts: top-level layout.js hatao, har route group ke andar ek layout.js jodo; har root layout ko apne khud ke <html> aur <body> tags chahiye. Poori tarah alag UI wale sections ke liye useful hai.

Dhyaan Do: kisi file ka naam page.js rakhne se route galti se public ho jata hai; future conventions ke saath naming collisions se bachna hai — internal files ke liye _ private folders use karo; components/lib folder ke naamo ka framework ke liye koi khaas mahatv nahi hai.

Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
route groups ( ) aur private folders _ me antar (groups organize karte hain + unka layout bhi ho sakta hai, aur unke children ab bhi routable hote hain; private folders routing ke liye invisible hote hain); colocation safe kyun hai (sirf page/route ki return value hi client ko bheji jati hai); rendering hierarchy ka order; multiple root layouts kaise kaam karte hain.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure
Hissa 04 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Layouts and Pages

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Layouts and Pages. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Layouts and Pages — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — file-system routing: folders route segments ko define karte hain jo URL segments par map hote hain; files (page, layout) kisi segment ke liye dikhaya jane wala UI banati hain.

Page banana: page woh UI hai jo ek specific route par render hota hai. app/ me ek page file jodo aur ek React component ko default export karo:

%
tsx
// app/page.tsx  →  /
export default function Page() {
  return <h1>Hello Next.js!</h1>
}
%

Layout banana: layout woh UI hai jo multiple pages ke beech shared hota hai. Navigation par layouts state preserve karte hain, interactive rehte hain, aur dobara render nahi hote. Ek layout file se React component ko default-export karo; ye ek children prop accept karta hai (ek page ya koi dusra layout):

%
tsx
// app/layout.tsx — root layout (required, must contain <html> and <body>)
export default function DashboardLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <main>{children}</main>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
%

Nested routes: /blog/[slug] = teen segments: / (Root Segment), blog (Segment), [slug] (Leaf Segment). Routes ko nest karne ke liye folders ko nest karo; kisi segment ko public banane ke liye page.tsx jodo:

%
tsx
// app/blog/page.tsx
import { getPosts } from '@/lib/posts'
import { Post } from '@/ui/post'

export default async function Page() {
  const posts = await getPosts()
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <Post key={post.id} post={post} />
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

Layouts ko nest karna: layouts children ke through nest hote hain — root layout blog layout ko wrap karta hai, aur blog layout page ko:

%
tsx
// app/blog/layout.tsx
export default function BlogLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <section>{children}</section>
}
%

Dynamic segments: data se routes generate karne ke liye folder ka naam square brackets [segmentName] me rakho:

%
tsx
// app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
export default async function BlogPostPage({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const post = await getPost(slug)
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
      <p>{post.content}</p>
    </div>
  )
}
%

CRITICAL (Next.js 15+): params ek Promise hai — tumhe await params karna hi hoga. Yahi baat searchParams par bhi lagu hoti hai. Dynamic segments me nested layouts bhi params access kar sakte hain.

Search params ke saath rendering: Server Component page me searchParams prop use karo:

%
tsx
export default async function Page({
  searchParams,
}: {
  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
}) {
  const filters = (await searchParams).filters
}
%

searchParams use karne se page dynamic rendering me opt-in ho jata hai (use incoming request chahiye hoti hai). Client Components search params ko useSearchParams hook se padhte hain.

Kab kya use karein:

  • searchParams prop — jab search params page ke liye data load karne ke kaam aayein (pagination, DB filtering).
  • useSearchParams — jab search params sirf client par use hon (pehle se load ki gayi list ko filter karna).
  • Optimization: callbacks/event handlers ke andar new URLSearchParams(window.location.search) bina re-render trigger kiye params padh deta hai.

Pages ke beech linking: next/link ka <Link> <a> ko prefetching + client-side navigation ke saath extend karta hai:

%
tsx
import Link from 'next/link'
export default async function Posts() {
  const posts = await getPosts()
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.slug}>
          <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

<Link> primary navigation method hai; useRouter advanced/programmatic navigation ke liye hai.

Route Props Helpers (typed, koi import nahi chahiye — globally available, next dev / next build / next typegen par generate hote hain):

%
tsx
// PageProps — params + searchParams inferred from the route
export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) {
  const { slug } = await props.params
  return <h1>Blog post: {slug}</h1>
}

// LayoutProps — children + named slots (e.g. app/dashboard/@analytics → props.analytics)
export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) {
  return <section>{props.children}</section>
}
%

Static routes ke liye params {} resolve hota hai.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Root layout required hai aur usme <html> + <body> hona hi chahiye.
  • Layouts navigation par rerender nahi hote (state preserve rehta hai — ye feature hai, lekin yahi wajah hai ki remount chahiye ho to template.js ki zaroorat padti hai).
  • params/searchParams Next.js 15+ me Promise hain — await bhoolna #1 migration bug hai.
  • searchParams use karne se page dynamic ban jata hai.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
layout banam page banam template (template remount hota hai, layout bana rehta hai); layouts navigation par state kyun preserve karte hain; params ka Promise hona (Next 15 ka breaking change); searchParams prop banam useSearchParams hook — kab kaunsa, aur dynamic rendering par iska asar.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages
Hissa 05 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Linking and Navigating

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Linking and Navigating. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Linking and Navigating — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Dynamic route without `loading.tsx`, Dynamic segment without `generateStaticParams`, Slow networks, Disabling prefetching, Hydration not completed. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — navigation kaise kaam karta hai (4 pillars):

1. Server Rendering: layouts/pages by default React Server Components hote hain. Initial aur uske baad ke har navigation par, Server Component Payload (RSC Payload) server par generate hokar client ko bheja jata hai. Do tarah ki rendering: Prerendering (build time par ya revalidation ke dauran, result cached) banam Dynamic Rendering (request time par). Initial visit ke liye HTML bhi generate hota hai. Trade-off: client ko server ka wait karna padta hai — prefetching + client-side transitions se ye wait kam ho jata hai.

2. Prefetching: user ke navigate karne se pehle hi route background me load ho jana. Next.js <Link> se jude routes ko automatic prefetch karta hai jab wo viewport me enter karte hain (ya hover par). Plain <a href> ko koi prefetching nahi milti. Kitna prefetch hoga, ye route par nirbhar karta hai: static route — poora route prefetch; dynamic route — prefetching skip, ya loading.tsx maujud ho to partially prefetched (shared layouts + loading skeleton pehle se). Skip karne se un routes par server ka kaam waste nahi hota jahan user kabhi jata hi nahi.

3. Streaming: server dynamic route ke hisse jaise-jaise taiyar hote hain, waise-waise bhej deta hai — poore route ka wait nahi karna padta. User ko jaldi kuch dikhne lagta hai. Ye loading.tsx se enable hota hai (Next.js page.tsx ko automatic ek <Suspense> boundary me wrap kar deta hai) ya components ke aas-paas manual <Suspense> se. Fayde: tatkal navigation + visual feedback, shared layouts interactive rehte hain, navigation interrupt ho sakti hai, behtar TTFB/FCP/TTI.

4. Client-side transitions: full page load (jo state saaf kar deta hai, scroll reset karta hai, interactivity block karta hai) ke bajay, <Link> shared layouts/UI ko rakhta hai aur page ko prefetched loading state ya naye page se replace kar deta hai. Server-rendered apps feel client-rendered apps jaisi hoti hain. Next.js transition par top par scroll karna sambhalta hai; sticky header ke peeche content chhup raha ho to CSS scroll-padding-top se theek karo.

Kya cheez transitions ko slow banati hai (aur uske fixes):

  • loading.tsx ke bina dynamic route: client server ka wait karta hai; unresponsive lagta hai. Fix: loading.tsx jodo (jaise app/blog/[slug]/loading.tsx jo ek skeleton return kare) → partial prefetch + tatkal navigation. Dev me DevTools + devIndicators static banam dynamic dikhate hain.
  • generateStaticParams ke bina dynamic segment: jo segment prerender ho sakta tha, wo dynamic rendering par gir jata hai. Fix: build time par saare params lane wala generateStaticParams jodo:
%
tsx
export async function generateStaticParams() {
  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
  return posts.map((post) => ({ slug: post.slug }))
}
%
  • Slow networks: ho sakta hai prefetch click se pehle khatm na ho; loading.js fallback bhi turant na dikhe. Fix: next/link ka useLinkStatus hook — transition pending ho to tatkal feedback dikhao:
%
tsx
'use client'
import { useLinkStatus } from 'next/link'

export default function LoadingIndicator() {
  const { pending } = useLinkStatus()
  return <span aria-hidden className={`link-hint ${pending ? 'is-pending' : ''}`} />
}
%
  • Hint ko debounce karo (jaise 100ms animation delay, shuruaat opacity: 0) taaki wo sirf slow navigations ke liye dikhe. Experimental useOffline hook connectivity girne ke dauran prefetched routes ko navigable rakhta hai. Dusre patterns: progress bars (jaise react-transition-progress).
  • Prefetching disable karna: <Link prefetch={false} href="/blog"> — badi link lists (infinite scroll tables) ke liye useful, taaki resources waste na hon. Trade-off: static route sirf click par fetch hoga; dynamic route ko pehle server par render hona hoga. Beech ka rasta — hover-only prefetch: prefetch={active ? null : false} aur onMouseEnter par active=true set karo.
  • Hydration pura nahi hua: <Link> ek Client Component hai aur prefetch karne se pehle use hydrate hona padta hai. Bade JS bundles hydration ko delay karte hain. Upay: bundles chhote karne ke liye @next/bundle-analyzer; logic ko client se server par le jao.

Native History API: Next.js window.history.pushState / replaceState ko router me integrate karta hai — URL badalne par usePathname/useSearchParams update ho jate hain. pushState ek history entry jodta hai (back button kaam karta hai — jaise ?sort=asc se products sort karna); replaceState current entry ko replace karta hai (koi back nahi — jaise locale switch /en/about → /fr/about). Tip: jab URL sirf ek event handler ko chahiye ho, to hooks ke bajay handler me window.location padho (dono hooks prerendering ko affect karte hain).

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • <a> tags ko na prefetch milta hai, na SPA transition — internal navigation ke liye hamesha <Link> use karo.
  • loading.tsx ke bina dynamic routes slow server par toote hue lagte hain.
  • Har jagah prefetch={false} lagane se instant feel khatm ho jati hai.
  • Kisi component me usePathname/useSearchParams use karna use dynamic rendering me opt-in kar deta hai.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
poori navigation pipeline samjhao (prefetch → RSC payload → streaming → client transition); static banam dynamic prefetch ka behaviour; loading.tsx partial prefetching kyun enable karta hai; generateStaticParams static/dynamic ka switch hai; slow-network feedback ke liye useLinkStatus; Next.js me pushState aur replaceState ka antar.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating
Hissa 06 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Server and Client Components

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Server and Client Components. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Server and Client Components — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: by default, layouts aur pages Server Components hote hain — data fetch karte hain aur server par render hote hain, optionally cache hote hain, aur client ko stream hote hain. Jab tumhe interactivity ya browser APIs chahiye hon, to Client Components use karo.

Client Components kab use karein: state + event handlers (onClick, onChange); lifecycle logic (useEffect); browser-only APIs (localStorage, window, navigator.geolocation); custom hooks.

Server Components kab use karein: source ke kareeb DB/API se data fetch karna; API keys/tokens/secrets ko expose kiye bina use karna; browser ko bheja jane wala JS kam karna; FCP behtar karna aur progressively stream karna.

Canonical pattern — server page data lata hai, client child interact karta hai:

%
tsx
// app/[id]/page.tsx — Server Component
import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'

export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = await params
  const post = await getPost(id)
  return (
    <div>
      <main>
        <h1>{post.title}</h1>
        <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
      </main>
    </div>
  )
}
% %
tsx
// app/ui/like-button.tsx — Client Component
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
export default function LikeButton({ likes }: { likes: number }) { /* ... */ }
%

Ye kaam kaise karta hai — server par: React APIs rendering ko orchestrate karti hain, aur kaam har route segment ke hisaab se chunks me banta hai (layouts, pages, parallel-route slots — chahe wo displayed hon ya na hon). Server Components RSC Payload (React Server Component Payload) me render hote hain; Client Components + RSC Payload ka use karke HTML prerender hota hai.

RSC Payload kya hai? Rendered Server Component tree ka ek compact serialized representation, jise client par React DOM update karne ke liye use karta hai. Isme hota hai: Server Components ka rendered result; un jagahon ke placeholders jahan Client Components render honge + unki JS files ke references; server se Client Components ko pass kiye gaye props.

Client par (first load): 1) HTML ek fast non-interactive preview dikhata hai; 2) RSC Payload client + server trees ko reconcile karta hai; 3) JS Client Components ko hydrate karta hai (hydration = static HTML ko interactive banane ke liye DOM me event handlers attach karna).

Uske baad ke navigations: RSC Payload tatkal navigation ke liye prefetched aur cached rehta hai; Client Components poori tarah client par render hote hain, bina server-rendered HTML ke.

"use client" directive: server aur client module graphs ke beech boundary declare karne ke liye file ke top par, imports ke upar rakho. Ek baar file mark ho jaye, to uske saare imports aur wo components jo wo directly render karta hai, client bundle me hote hain — har client component par directive lagane ki zaroorat nahi. Ye un Server Components par lagu nahi hota jo children/props ke roop me pass hote hain — wo server par render hote hain aur rendered output ke roop me aate hain.

JS bundle size kam karna: 'use client' bade wrapper par nahi, leaf interactive component par lagao. Jaise ek server Layout jisme static logo/nav + interactive <Search /> hai: sirf search.tsx ko 'use client' milega; baaki server-rendered rahega.

Data pass karna Server → Client: props ke through — lekin props React ke dwara serializable hone chahiye. Dusra tareeka: React ke use API se data stream karo (ek un-awaited promise ko prop ke roop me pass karo; client use <Suspense> ke andar use() se padhta hai).

Interleaving (children slot pattern): Server Components ko Client Components ke props/children ke roop me pass karo — jaise ek client <Modal> (state visibility toggle karti hai) apne child ke roop me ek server <Cart> (data fetch karta hai) receive karta hai. Server Components server par pehle se render ho jate hain, tab bhi jab wo Client Components ko pass kiye jate hain.

%
tsx
// app/ui/modal.tsx — 'use client'
export default function Modal({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <div>{children}</div>
}
// app/page.tsx — Server Component
import Modal from './ui/modal'
import Cart from './ui/cart'
export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Modal>
      <Cart />
    </Modal>
  )
}
%

Context providers: React context Server Components me supported nahi hai. Pattern: ek Client Component provider banao jo children accept kare, use kisi Server Component (jaise layout) me import karo. Providers ko tree me jitna deep ho sake render karo (sirf {children} ko wrap karo, poore <html> ko nahi) taaki Next.js static hisson ko optimize kar sake. Server se fetch kiya data context ke through pass karne ke liye, Context Provider ke andar React ka use use karo (SPAs guide dekho).

Third-party components: agar koi library component client-only features use karta hai lekin usme "use client" nahi hai, to wo Server Component me error dega. Fix: use apne khud ke Client Component me wrap karo ('use client' + re-export). Library authors ko client-only features use karne wale entry points par "use client" jodna chahiye (note: kuch bundlers directive ko strip kar dete hain — react-wrap-balancer / vercel/analytics repos me esbuild config ke udaharan hain).

Environment poisoning se bachna: modules server aur client graphs ke beech share ho sakte hain — server-only code (jaise process.env.API_KEY use karne wala function) galti se client me import karna aasan hai. Sirf NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed env vars client bundle me shamil hote hain; baaki empty string se replace ho jate hain (isliye code client par chupchap fail ho jata hai). server-only package se guard karo: server-only files me import 'server-only' → agar Client Component me import hua to build-time error. client-only iska ulta hai, client-only logic (jaise window) ke liye. Install karna optional hai; Next.js in imports ko internally handle karta hai taaki errors saaf milein, aur apni type declarations bhi deta hai (noUncheckedSideEffectImports on ho to ye relevant hai).

%
js
// lib/data.js
import 'server-only'
export async function getData() {
  const res = await fetch('https://external-service.com/data', {
    headers: { authorization: process.env.API_KEY },
  })
  return res.json()
}
%

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Poore layout ko 'use client' mark karne se bundle phool jata hai — leaves ko mark karo.
  • Client Components ko diye jane wale props serializable hone chahiye (koi functions, Dates, class instances nahi).
  • Context Server Components me directly kaam nahi karta.
  • server-only import tabhi build error deta hai jab tum use asal me use karo.
  • NEXT_PUBLIC_ ke bina wale env vars client par empty string ban jate hain (silent failure, error nahi).
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
RSC Payload me kya hota hai; hydration banam prerendering banam streaming; "use client" ki module-graph boundary wali semantics (children/props boundary se bahar nikal jate hain); interleaving pattern; Server Components FCP aur security kyun behtar karte hain; server-only/client-only build-time guards ke roop me.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components
Hissa 07 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Fetching Data

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Fetching Data. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Fetching Data — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Sequential, Parallel. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — Server Components kisi bhi async I/O ke saath fetch karte hain:

1. fetch API — component ko async banao aur await fetch(...) karo:

%
tsx
export default async function Page() {
  const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog')
  const posts = await data.json()
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

Jaanna achha rahega: ek hi component tree me identical fetch requests by default memoized hoti hain (data usi component me fetch karo jise uski zaroorat hai, koi prop drilling nahi); fetch requests by default cached nahi hotin aur poori hone tak page ko render hone se rokti hain — cache karne ke liye 'use cache' use karo, ya stream karne ke liye <Suspense> me wrap karo; dev me fetch logging logging config se milti hai.

2. ORM / database — Server Components server par chalte hain, isliye credentials/query logic kabhi client bundle me nahi jati:

%
tsx
import { db, posts } from '@/lib/db'
export default async function Page() {
  const allPosts = await db.select().from(posts)
  return (
    <ul>
      {allPosts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

Phir bhi requests ko theek se authenticate/authorize karo (Data Security guide dekho).

Streaming — slow data ke poore route ko block karne ka fix: page ko progressively bheje jane wale chunks me todo. Do tareeke:

1. loading.js — poore page ko stream karta hai. Page ke bagal me app/blog/loading.tsx jodo; Next.js page.js ko automatic <Suspense> me wrap kar deta hai. Navigation par user ko turant layout + loading state dikhta hai; taiyar hone par content swap ho jata hai. Caveat: loading.js layout.js ke andar nested hota hai, isliye jo layout uncached/runtime data (cookies(), headers(), uncached fetch) access karta hai, wo usi segment ke loading.js par fallback nahi karta — wo layout ke render hone tak navigation ko block karta hai. Fix: uncached access ko uski apni <Suspense> me fallback ke saath wrap karo, ya fetching ko page.js me le jao. Cache Components is situation ko build-time error se rokta hai. Rule of thumb: uncached data ke kareeb <Suspense> rakhna, loading.js par bharosa karne se behtar hai.

2. Kisi component ke aas-paas <Suspense> — granular streaming; boundary ke bahar ki content turant ship ho jati hai:

%
tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import BlogList from '@/components/BlogList'
import BlogListSkeleton from '@/components/BlogListSkeleton'

export default function BlogPage() {
  return (
    <div>
      <header>
        <h1>Welcome to the Blog</h1>
        <p>Read the latest posts below.</p>
      </header>
      <main>
        <Suspense fallback={<BlogListSkeleton />}>
          <BlogList />
        </Suspense>
      </main>
    </div>
  )
}
%

Meaningful loading states: skeletons/spinners, ya future screen ka ek chhota meaningful hissa (cover photo, title). Dev me React DevTools se preview karo. Bots/crawlers: Next.js unhe stream nahi karta — wo data ka wait karke poora rendered page bhejta hai (SEO-safe).

Client Components — do tareeke:

1. React use API — server par fetch karo, un-awaited promise ko prop ke roop me pass karo, client me use <Suspense> ke andar use() se padho:

%
tsx
// Server: app/blog/page.tsx
import Posts from '@/app/ui/posts'
import { Suspense } from 'react'
export default function Page() {
  const posts = getPosts() // Don't await
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
      <Posts posts={posts} />
    </Suspense>
  )
}
// Client: app/ui/posts.tsx
'use client'
import { use } from 'react'
export default function Posts({ posts }: { posts: Promise<{ id: string; title: string }[]> }) {
  const allPosts = use(posts)
  return (
    <ul>
      {allPosts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

Ek hi promise ko kai Client Components ke saath share karne ke liye, use context ke through provide karo (SPAs guide dekho).

2. Community libraries — SWR ya React Query (TanStack Query), apni khud ki caching/streaming semantics ke saath:

%
tsx
'use client'
import useSWR from 'swr'
const fetcher = (url) => fetch(url).then((r) => r.json())
export default function BlogPage() {
  const { data, error, isLoading } = useSWR('https://api.vercel.app/blog', fetcher)
  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>
  if (error) return <div>Error: {error.message}</div>
  return (
    <ul>
      {data.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

Sequential banam parallel fetching:

  • Sequential (dependent): jaise <Playlists> ko getArtist() se mili artist.id chahiye — ye unavoidable hai, lekin dependent hisse ko <Suspense> me wrap karo taaki wo pehli request ke baad stream-in ho jaye. Pehli request sab kuch block karti hai — use optimize karo ya cache karo.
  • Parallel (independent): layouts aur pages by default parallel render hote hain, LEKIN ek hi component ke andar sequential awaits sequential hi rehte hain. Fix — pehle requests start karo, phir await Promise.all karo:
%
tsx
const artistData = getArtist(username)
const albumsData = getAlbums(username)
const [artist, albums] = await Promise.all([artistData, albumsData])
%

Agar ek request fail ho jaye, to Promise.all sab fail kar deta hai — individual failures ko tolerate karne ke liye Promise.allSettled use karo.

React.cache se data reuse karna: non-fetch access (ORM/DB) ke liye, function ko React.cache me wrap karo taaki ek hi request me kai components ek hi result share karein:

%
ts
import { cache } from 'react'
export const getUser = cache(async (id: string) => {
  return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) })
})
%

React.cache sirf current request tak scoped hai — requests ke beech koi sharing nahi.

Data preload karna (waterfalls se bachna): jab koi component dusre blocking kaam ke baad render hota hai, to uski request der se start hoti hai. Blocking kaam se pehle fetcher ko bina await kiye call karo (void getItem(id)), phir use consuming component me dobara call karo — deduplication (automatic fetch memoization, React.cache, ya request APIs ke liye 'use cache' / 'use cache: private') shuru ki gayi request ko hi reuse kar leta hai. preload function ko consuming component ke paas hi rakho.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • fetch by default cached nahi hota (Next.js 15+ ka naya default).
  • loading.js un layouts ko cover nahi karta jo runtime data padhte hain.
  • Promise.all all-or-nothing hai.
  • React.cache per-request hai, cross-request cache nahi.
  • Bots ko streams nahi, poori rendered pages milti hain.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
server-side fetching secrets ke liye safe kyun hai; memoization banam caching (alag layers); sequential banam parallel patterns aur waterfall; React.cache ka maksad; preloading pattern; use() promise-streaming pattern; server fetching ke bajay SWR/React Query kab use karein.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data
Hissa 08 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Mutating Data

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Mutating Data. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Mutating Data — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Refresh the current page, Revalidate cache, Redirect, Cookies, `useEffect` invocation. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — Server Functions / Server Actions: ek Server Function server par chalne wala async function hai, jo client se ek network request ke through call kiya ja sakta hai (isiliye async hona zaroori hai). Action/mutation ke context me ise Server Action kehte hain. Convention ke hisaab se, Server Action woh async function hai jo startTransition ke saath use hota hai — ye automatic ho jata hai jab use <form> ko action prop se ya <button> ko formAction se pass kiya jata hai. Invoke hone par, Next.js updated UI aur naya data dono ek single server roundtrip me wapas kar sakta hai. Peeche se actions POST method use karte hain — sirf POST hi inhe invoke kar sakta hai.

Security warning (critical): Server Functions tak direct POST requests se bhi pahuncha ja sakta hai, sirf tumhare UI se nahi. Har Server Function ke andar hamesha authentication aur authorization verify karo. Kisi resource ko delete/mutate karne se pehle ye bhi verify karo ki user us resource ka owner hai.

Server Functions banana — 'use server' directive: kisi async function ke top par lagao, ya file ke top par lagao taaki uske saare exports mark ho jayein:

%
ts
// app/lib/actions.ts
import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'

export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
  'use server'
  const session = await auth()
  if (!session?.user) {
    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
  }
  const title = formData.get('title')
  const content = formData.get('content')
  // Mutate data
  // Revalidate cache
}
%

Server Components me: function body ke top par 'use server' jodkar inline define karo. Server Components by default progressive enhancement support karte hain — Server Actions ko call karne wale forms tab bhi submit ho jate hain jab JS load na hua ho ya disabled ho.

Client Components me: tum wahan Server Functions define nahi kar sakte, lekin unhe invoke kar sakte ho — kisi aisi file se import karke jiske top par 'use server' ho:

%
ts
// app/actions.ts
'use server'
export async function createPost() {}
% %
tsx
// app/ui/button.tsx
'use client'
import { createPost } from '@/app/actions'
export function Button() {
  return <button formAction={createPost}>Create</button>
}
%

Client Components me, agar JS abhi load nahi hua hai to form submissions queue ho jati hain aur hydration ke liye prioritize hoti hain; hydration ke baad browser submit par refresh nahi hota. Actions ko props ke roop me bhi Client Components ko pass kiya ja sakta hai (<ClientComponent updateItemAction={updateItem} />).

Invoke karna — do main tareeke:

1. Forms (Server + Client Components): React <form> ko extend karta hai taaki ek Server Function ko action prop ke roop me pass kiya ja sake; use automatic ek FormData object milta hai:

%
tsx
import { createPost } from '@/app/actions'
export function Form() {
  return (
    <form action={createPost}>
      <input type="text" name="title" />
      <input type="text" name="content" />
      <button type="submit">Create</button>
    </form>
  )
}
%

2. Event handlers / useEffect Client Components me: onClick wagera:

%
tsx
'use client'
import { incrementLike } from './actions'
import { useState } from 'react'

export default function LikeButton({ initialLikes }: { initialLikes: number }) {
  const [likes, setLikes] = useState(initialLikes)
  return (
    <>
      <p>Total Likes: {likes}</p>
      <button
        onClick={async () => {
          const updatedLikes = await incrementLike()
          setLikes(updatedLikes)
        }}
      >
        Like
      </button>
    </>
  )
}
%

Note: client Server Functions ko ek-ek karke dispatch aur await karta hai (sequential dispatch). Parallel kaam ke liye, use ek hi Server Function ya Route Handler ke andar karo, ya server-side data fetching use karo.

Pending state — useActionState:

%
tsx
'use client'
import { useActionState, startTransition } from 'react'
import { createPost } from '@/app/actions'

export function Button() {
  const [state, action, pending] = useActionState(createPost, false)
  return (
    <button onClick={() => startTransition(action)}>
      {pending ? <LoadingSpinner /> : 'Create Post'}
    </button>
  )
}
%

Experimental useOffline ke saath, connectivity girne se ruka hua action pending rehta hai aur network wapas aane par pura ho jata hai.

Mutation ke baad — refresh / revalidate / redirect / cookies:

  • Current page refresh karna — Server Action me next/cache ka refresh() router ko dobara render karta hai taaki UI latest state dikhaye. Ye tagged data ko revalidate nahi karta (uske liye updateTag/revalidateTag use karo).
  • Cache revalidate karna — mutate karne ke baad next/cache se revalidatePath('/posts') ya revalidateTag('posts').
  • Redirect — next/navigation se redirect('/posts'). Ye ek framework-handled control-flow exception throw karta hai — uske baad ka code kabhi execute nahi hota, isliye revalidatePath/revalidateTag ko redirect se PEHLE call karo.
  • Cookies — next/headers se cookies() (await cookies(), phir .get()/.set()/.delete()). Server Action me cookie set/delete karne se current page + layouts server par dobara render hote hain taaki UI nayi value dikhaye; re-render hone wale components ka client state preserve rehta hai, aur deps badle hon to effects dobara chalte hain.
  • useEffect se invocation — jaise mount par view count badhana, ya global events (keyboard shortcuts, infinite scroll ke liye intersection observer) par trigger karna; call ko startTransition me wrap karo aur feedback ke liye useTransition ka isPending use karo.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • UI par kabhi bharosa mat karo — har action ke andar auth rakho.
  • redirect() throw karta hai (uske baad kuch nahi chalta).
  • refresh() tags ko revalidate nahi karta.
  • Actions client par sequential hote hain.
  • Server Functions Client Components me define nahi ho sakte.
  • FormData.get() FormDataEntryValue | null return karta hai — validate karo.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
Server Function banam Server Action ki terminology (action = mutation/form context me use hone wala Server Function); sirf POST se invocation; progressive enhancement; single-roundtrip UI+data response; useActionState pending pattern; revalidate-phir-redirect ka order; auth action ke andar hi kyun hona chahiye.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data
Hissa 09 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Caching

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Caching. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Caching — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Data-level, UI-level, Prerendered output, Shared store, Browser. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: caching data fetching/computation ke result ko store karta hai taaki usi data ke liye future requests bina kaam dobara kiye, tezi se serve ho jayein. Note: ye page Cache Components (next.config.ts me cacheComponents: true) wali caching cover karta hai. Uske bina ke model ke liye "Caching (Previous Model)" guide dekho.

Cache Components enable karna: create-next-app se bane naye apps me recommended defaults ke saath Cache Components + Partial Prefetching pehle se enabled hote hain. Existing/manual apps ke liye:

%
ts
// next.config.ts
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}
export default nextConfig
%

partialPrefetching ko explicitly set karo — unset chhodne par warning log hoti hai (Cache Components ki pehli release me ye nahi tha). false sirf tab set karo jab tum kisi aise app ko migrate kar rahe ho jisne Partial Prefetching se pehle Cache Components apnaya tha. Agli major release me dono har jagah enabled honge aur ye options hat jayenge. Cache Components ke saath, GET Route Handlers bhi pages wala hi prerendering model follow karte hain.

'use cache' directive — do levels:

  • Data-level: data fetch/compute karne wale function ko cache karo (getProducts(), getUser(id)).
  • UI-level: poore component/page/layout ko cache karo (async function BlogPosts()).

Ek cache directive result ko ek lifetime deta hai, jo time-based revalidation aur rendering optimizations ke liye use hoti hai. Har cache directive ke saath ek cacheLife jodo. Arguments + parent scope se capture ki gayi values automatic cache key ka hissa ban jati hain (alag inputs → alag entries). File ke top par 'use cache' lagane se us file ke saare exported functions cache ho jate hain.

%
tsx
// Data-level
import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
export async function getUsers() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')
  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
}

// UI-level
export default async function Page() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')
  const users = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
  return (
    <ul>
      {users.map((user) => (
        <li key={user.id}>{user.name}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
%

Uncached data ko stream karna: jo data har request par fresh hona chahiye, uske liye 'use cache' mat use karo. Component ko ek fallback ke saath <Suspense> me wrap karo — fallback prerendered shell ke saath ship ho jata hai jabki async kaam request time par chalta hai. Uncached read ke aas-paas <Suspense> boundary na ho to dev overlay ek blocking-route insight dikhata hai jiska fix hai "Wrap in or move into Suspense". Note: sirf <Suspense> kisi component ko dynamic rendering me opt-in nahi karta — poori tarah synchronous kaam <Suspense> ke andar bhi prerendering ke dauran hi pura ho jata hai.

Runtime APIs (sirf request time par maloom hoti hain): cookies(), headers(), searchParams, params (known values ko prerender karne ke liye generateStaticParams use karo, ya unknown values ke liye Cache Components ke saath ISR). Runtime APIs access karne wale components ko <Suspense> me wrap karna chahiye — <Suspense> boundary ke andar cookies() padhna poore route ko dynamic rendering me opt-in nahi karta, purane model ki tarah; static + cached content initial HTML me phir bhi ship hota hai.

'use cache: private': un functions ke liye variant jo cookies/headers/searchParams ko directly padhte hain — inhe ek lifetime deta hai taaki ye kisi prefetch me shamil ho sakein. Dusra pattern — runtime value ko extract karke ek shared cached function ko argument ke roop me pass karo:

%
tsx
async function ProfileContent() {
  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
  return <CachedContent sessionId={session} />
}
async function CachedContent({ sessionId }: { sessionId: string }) {
  'use cache'
  // sessionId becomes part of the cache key
  const data = await fetchUserData(sessionId)
  return <div>{data}</div>
}
%

Caveat: kyunki ye request data ke peeche gated hai, ye prerendered static shell me nahi hota; runtime par ye by default in-memory cached rehta hai (serverless par ephemeral — har request par dobara evaluate ho sakta hai). Durable shared caching ke liye 'use cache: remote' use karo.

Static + cached + streaming ek saath (ek page me): static header prerendered; 'use cache' + cacheLife('hours') + cacheTag('posts') wala <BlogPosts /> static shell me shamil; cookies() padhne wala <UserPreferences /> <Suspense> ke peeche stream hota hai. Failures ko error boundaries rok ti hain: catchError (component-level) ya error.js (route-level). Yahi insights generateMetadata/generateViewport ke andar bhi lagu hoti hain.

Random values aur timestamps: Math.random(), Date.now(), crypto.randomUUID() har execution par alag hote hain — Cache Components inke liye explicit handling mangta hai. Do options: (a) per-request unique value — operation se pehle connection() (next/server se) call karo aur <Suspense> me wrap karo; (b) result ko cache karo — 'use cache' taaki revalidation tak saare users ko ek hi value dikhe. performance.now() telemetry ke liye hai aur guarded nahi hai. Dev overlay fixes ke saath blocking-prerender-random / -current-time / -crypto insights dikhata hai.

Predictable values: module imports, sync I/O (fs.readFileSync), pure computations har baar ek hi result dete hain → automatic static shell me prerender ho jate hain. Isme sync embedded-DB queries (better-sqlite3, node:sqlite) bhi shamil hain; sync source se per-request data chahiye to pehle connection() call karo. Request-independent resources (fonts, config files) ki async reads rendering ke dauran nahi, module scope par ek baar honi chahiye; ya render ke dauran compute hokar reuse hon to 'use cache' me wrap karo; request-time rendering ke dauran sirf tab padho jab wo request-dependent hon ya badalte hon.

Prerendering / Partial Prerendering (PPR): build time par Next.js route ke component tree ko render karta hai: 'use cache' results cached hokar static shell me shamil hote hain (agar lifetime bahut chhoti na ho); <Suspense> fallbacks shamil hote hain jabki content stream hota hai; predictable values prerender ke dauran pure ho jate hain; random values ko connection() + <Suspense> ya 'use cache' chahiye. Static shell = direct visits ke liye HTML + client navigation ke liye serialized RSC Payload. Cache Components ke saath PPR default hai. Har static shell bina origin ko hit kiye seedha CDN se serve ho sakta hai — direct navigations tatkal hoti hain. Jab dynamic params known hon (generateStaticParams se), to shell me concrete content hota hai; jab unknown hon, to reusable URL-independent version App Shell hota hai (param-specific hisse fallbacks ke peeche); ISR pehli visit ke baad concrete versions bhar deta hai. Next.js routes ko build/dev par validate karta hai: jo components prerendering ke dauran pure nahi ho sakte, unke liye dev-overlay insight route ka naam + fixes (cache karo, Suspense karo, ya opt out karo) deta hai — isse har route ek static shell produce karta hai.

Static shell ko maximize karna — key structural pattern: async kaam tree me jitna deep baitha ho, page ka utna zyada hissa prerender ho sakta hai. Layout level par await params mat karo (agar param dynamic hai to ye poore layout ko prerender hone se rok dega); iske bajay promise ko neeche pass karo aur <Suspense> boundary ke andar await karo:

%
tsx
// Not async: layout never awaits params
export default function Layout({ children, params }: LayoutProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) {
  return (
    <div>
      <Sidebar />
      <Suspense fallback={<h1>Loading...</h1>}>
        {params.then(({ slug }) => (
          <SlugHeading slug={slug} />
        ))}
      </Suspense>
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}
%

Yahi principle cookies(), headers(), searchParams aur fetches par bhi lagu hota hai. "Optimizing the static shell" guide dekho.

Tatkal navigation: Cache Components client navigations ko bhi validate karta hai (sirf direct visits ko nahi) — insights/errors tumhe data ko <Suspense> me wrap karne, use cache se cache karne, ya access ko move karne ki taraf guide karte hain.

Prefetching (Partial Prefetching): router by default har route ka App Shell prefetch karta hai (static content + cookies()/headers() se session data). Kisi link ke URL data (searchParams, dynamic params) par nirbhar cached content bhi prefetch karna ho to us link par prefetch={true} set karo — Next.js prefetch time par destination URL ko resolve karke route ke tree ko dobara render karta hai; runtime-extracted args wala 'use cache' aur 'use cache: private' per-link prefetch me shamil ho jate hain; <Suspense> fallbacks prefetched UI me rehte hain. Cost: har prefetchable link ke liye ek server invocation.

Cached content kahan store hota hai: output ek RSC payload me serialize hota hai; cacheLife tay karta hai ki har copy kitni der fresh rahegi:

  • Prerendered output: HTML + RSC payload disk par (self-hosted) ya CDN ke peeche durable platform storage me. revalidate/expire rebuilds ko control karte hain.
  • Shared store: by default per-instance in-memory (serverless par ephemeral); 'use cache: remote' use durable cache handler me le jata hai jo instances ke beech shared hota hai (network roundtrip — sirf high hit rate par fayda).
  • Browser: payload navigation/prefetch ke liye RSC me shamil, apne stale window tak fresh; 'use cache: private' results sirf yahin rehte hain.
  • Session-specific App Shells (cookies()/headers() padhne wale) client par per-session cached hote hain, shared server cache me nahi.
  • Saare stores ek hi deployment tak scoped hote hain — naya deploy fresh shuru hota hai; cache keys me build id shamil hota hai, isliye remote entries bhi carry over nahi hotin.

ISR: generateStaticParams listed URLs ko build par prerender karta hai; dusri URLs ko App Shell tatkal milta hai, phir known params ke saath background me upgrade hokar agle visitor ke liye cache ho jati hain.

Bots aur crawlers: PPR ke saath metadata dynamic ho sakta hai jabki page prerendered ho; kuch bots ye handle nahi kar sakte aur unhe metadata <head> me chahiye. Next.js user agent se inhe detect karta hai, static shell skip karta hai, aur request time par dynamically render karta hai. Build-time prerender ke liye available data sources request time par bhi available hone chahiye, warna bots ko 500 milega.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • cacheLife bhool jana (implicit default profile lagu ho jata hai — use explicitly jodo).
  • Runtime APIs padhne wale function par bina : private variant ke 'use cache' lagana.
  • Tree me upar ki taraf params/cookies() ko await karna static shell ko khatm kar deta hai.
  • In-memory cache serverless par persist nahi hota.
  • Short-lived caches prerenders se exclude ho jate hain.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
Cache Components banam previous model; data-level banam UI-level caching; cache key ki composition (args + captured values); App Shell banam static shell banam concrete page; PPR ka default hona; "async kaam ko tree me neeche dhakelo" wala pattern; har cache store kahan rehta hai aur uski lifetime semantics.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching
Hissa 10 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Revalidating

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Revalidating. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Revalidating — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: revalidation ka matlab hai cached data ko update karna — tez cached responses serve karte raho, lekin content fresh bhi rakho. Do strategies: time-based (automatic, cacheLife se) aur on-demand (manual, revalidateTag / updateTag / revalidatePath se). Note: ye page Cache Components wali revalidation cover karta hai. Uske bina ke model ke liye "Caching (Previous Model)" dekho.

cacheLife profiles (stale / revalidate / expire):

Profilestalerevalidateexpire
default5m15mkabhi nahi
seconds30s1s60s
minutes5m1m1h
hours5m1h1d
days5m1d1w
weeks5m1w30d
max5m30d1y

Custom object form:

%
tsx
'use cache'
cacheLife({
  stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
  revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
  expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
})
%

Short-lived caches (seconds profile, revalidate: 0, ya 5 minute se kam expire) automatic prerenders se exclude ho jate hain aur iske bajay dynamic holes ban jate hain.

cacheTag: 'use cache' scope ke andar cached data ko tag karo taaki use on-demand invalidate kiya ja sake:

%
tsx
import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
export async function getProducts() {
  'use cache'
  cacheTag('products')
  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
}
%

revalidateTag(tag, 'max'): tag ke hisaab se stale-while-revalidate semantics ke saath invalidate karta hai — stale content turant serve hota hai jabki fresh content background me generate hota hai. Blogs/catalogs ke liye ideal, jahan halki si deri chalegi. Dusra argument = fresh generate hote samay stale content kitni der serve ho sakta hai; expire ho jane ke baad, fresh taiyar hone tak requests block hoti hain. 'max' = sabse lamba stale window. Kai functions me ek hi tag ho to wo sab ek saath revalidate ho jate hain. Server Actions ya Route Handlers me call kiya ja sakta hai.

updateTag(tag): cached data ko turant expire kar deta hai — read-your-own-writes ke liye (user ko apna change fauran dikhe). Sirf Server Actions me. Ye calling route ko refresh bhi karta hai aur client cache entries ko invalidate bhi.

%
tsx
import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
  const post = await db.post.create({ data: { title: formData.get('title'), content: formData.get('content') } })
  updateTag('posts')
  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
}
%
updateTagrevalidateTag(tag, 'max')
Kahansirf Server ActionsServer Actions + Route Handlers
Behaviourturant expirestale-while-revalidate
Use caseread-your-own-writesbackground refresh, halki deri OK

revalidatePath(path): kisi route path ka saara cached data invalidate kar deta hai — tab use karo jab tumhe na pata ho ki kaunse tags jude hain. Jahan mumkin ho, tag-based revalidation ko preference do: tags server cache ko zyada precisely target karte hain aur over-invalidation se bachate hain.

%
tsx
import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
export async function updateUser(id: string) {
  // Mutate data
  revalidatePath('/profile')
}
%

Kya cache karna chahiye? Woh data jo runtime data par nirbhar nahi karta aur jise tum kuch der cache se serve karne par raazi ho — use cache + cacheLife. CMS content ke liye jise time-based revalidation nahi chahiye: cacheTag + max jaisi lambi cacheLife rakho taaki wo static shell me rahe, aur CMS ko change par revalidateTag call karne wala webhook trigger karne do — isse bekaar ki time-based revalidation bachti hai. Note: serverless me in-memory cache entries revalidations ke paar persist nahi bhi ho sakti.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • updateTag sirf Server Actions me hai (Route Handlers me nahi).
  • revalidatePath tags ke muqable over-invalidate karta hai.
  • Short-lived cacheLife profiles content ko chupchap prerenders se bahar kar dete hain.
  • Tag karna bhool gaye to sirf path se hi revalidate kar paoge.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
stale banam revalidate banam expire ki semantics; SWR banam turant expiry; teeno invalidation functions me se kab kaunsa use karein; CMS webhook + cacheTag('...') + cacheLife('max') wala pattern; tags paths se behtar kyun hain.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating
Hissa 11 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Error Handling

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Error Handling. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Error Handling — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — do categories:

1. Expected errors — normal operation ke dauran hote hain (server-side form validation, failed requests). Inhe explicitly handle karo aur client ko wapas bhejo.

2. Uncaught exceptions — unexpected bugs. Inhe throw karke handle karo; ye error boundaries ke dwara pakde jate hain.

Expected errors — Server Functions: useActionState use karo; expected errors ko return values ke roop me model karo, try/catch + throw se nahi:

%
ts
// app/actions.ts
'use server'
export async function createPost(prevState: any, formData: FormData) {
  const title = formData.get('title')
  const content = formData.get('content')
  const res = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/posts', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: { title, content },
  })
  const json = await res.json()
  if (!res.ok) {
    return { message: 'Failed to create post' }
  }
}
% %
tsx
// app/ui/form.tsx — 'use client'
import { useActionState } from 'react'
import { createPost } from '@/app/actions'
const initialState = { message: '' }
export function Form() {
  const [state, formAction, pending] = useActionState(createPost, initialState)
  return (
    <form action={formAction}>
      <label htmlFor="title">Title</label>
      <input type="text" id="title" name="title" required />
      <label htmlFor="content">Content</label>
      <textarea id="content" name="content" required />
      {state?.message && <p aria-live="polite">{state.message}</p>}
      <button disabled={pending}>Create Post</button>
    </form>
  )
}
%

Expected errors — Server Components: response ko check karo aur conditionally error message render karo ya redirect() karo:

%
tsx
export default async function Page() {
  const res = await fetch(`https://...`)
  const data = await res.json()
  if (!res.ok) {
    return 'There was an error.'
  }
  return '...'
}
%

Not found: kisi route segment me notFound() (next/navigation se) call karo + 404 UI ke liye ek not-found.js file rakho:

%
tsx
// app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const post = getPostBySlug(slug)
  if (!post) {
    notFound()
  }
  return <div>{post.title}</div>
}
// app/blog/[slug]/not-found.tsx
export default function NotFound() {
  return <div>404 - Page Not Found</div>
}
%

Uncaught exceptions — nested error boundaries: kisi route segment me error.js jodo; ye Client Component hona hi chahiye ('use client'), ise { error, retry } props milte hain; retry() segment ko dobara fetch aur re-render karta hai. Error ko useEffect me log karo (jaise kisi error-reporting service ko). Errors sabse kareeb ke parent error boundary tak bubble hote hain — granular handling ke liye error.tsx ko hierarchy ke alag-alag levels par rakho.

%
tsx
// app/dashboard/error.tsx
'use client'
import { useEffect } from 'react'
export default function ErrorPage({ error, retry }: { error: unknown; retry: () => void }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    console.error(error)
  }, [error])
  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Something went wrong!</h2>
      <button onClick={() => retry()}>Try again</button>
    </div>
  )
}
%

Component-level boundaries — catchError: next/error ka catchError tree ke kisi bhi hisse ko wrap karta hai (sirf route segments ko nahi):

%
tsx
'use client'
import { catchError, type ErrorInfo } from 'next/error'
function ErrorFallback(props: { title: string }, { error, retry }: ErrorInfo) {
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
  return (
    <div>
      <h2>{props.title}</h2>
      <p>{message}</p>
      <button onClick={() => retry()}>Try again</button>
    </div>
  )
}
export default catchError(ErrorFallback)
// Usage: <ErrorBoundary title="Dashboard Error">{children}</ErrorBoundary>
%

Error boundaries event handlers ke errors ko pakadti NAHI hain (wo rendering ke baad chalte hain). Unhe manually try/catch + useState/useReducer se handle karo — error ko store karke fallback UI render karo. Exception: useTransition ke startTransition ke andar ke unhandled errors sabse kareeb ki error boundary tak bubble hote hain.

Global errors — global-error.js: root app directory me hota hai; root layout ke andar ke errors ko pakadta hai. Ise apne khud ke <html> aur <body> tags define karne hote hain (active hone par ye root layout ko replace kar deta hai). i18n setups ke saath bhi kaam karta hai.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • 'use client' ke bina error.js kaam nahi karega.
  • Error boundaries event-handler errors pakdengi, ye ummeed rakhna galat hai (wo nahi pakadti).
  • notFound() banam throw karna — notFound() not-found.js render karta hai, error.js nahi.
  • retry() sirf segment ko dobara render karta hai, asal bug ko theek nahi karta.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
expected banam uncaught errors ki taxonomy; Server Actions throw karne ke bajay error state kyun return karte hain; error boundary ka bubbling + granularity; catchError banam error.js; global-error.js ko apne html/body kyun chahiye; event-handler errors ko handle karne ka pattern.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling
Hissa 12 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

CSS

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai CSS. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: CSS — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — style karne ke chhe tareeke: Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules, Global CSS, External Stylesheets, Sass, CSS-in-JS.

Tailwind CSS (v4, default):

%
bash
npm install -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss
% %
js
// postcss.config.mjs
export default {
  plugins: { '@tailwindcss/postcss': {} },
}
% %
css
/* app/globals.css */
@import 'tailwindcss';
%

CSS ko root layout me import karo (import './globals.css'), phir utility classes use karo (className="flex min-h-screen flex-col items-center justify-between p-24"). Bahut purane browsers ke liye Tailwind v3 guide dekho.

CSS Modules: locally scoped CSS — unique class names generate hoti hain, isliye alag files me ek hi class name kabhi takrata nahi. File ka naam .module.css par khatm hona chahiye, aur ise app me kahin bhi import kar sakte ho:

%
css
/* app/blog/blog.module.css */
.blog {
  padding: 24px;
}
% %
tsx
import styles from './blog.module.css'
export default function Page() {
  return <main className={styles.blog}></main>
}
%

Global CSS: root layout me import ki gayi app/global.css har route par lagu hoti hai. Caveat: Next.js React ke built-in stylesheet support ko Suspense ke saath integrate karke use karta hai — tumhare navigate karne par stylesheets remove nahi hotin, jisse conflicts ho sakte hain. Salah: global styles sirf sach me global CSS ke liye (jaise Tailwind base), component styling ke liye Tailwind, aur custom scoped CSS ke liye CSS Modules.

External stylesheets: app me kahin bhi import karo, colocated components me bhi — jaise import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.css'. React 19 me <link rel="stylesheet" href="..." /> bhi use kiya ja sakta hai.

Ordering aur merging: Next.js production me CSS ko optimize karta hai — stylesheets ko automatic chunk/merge karke. CSS ka order code me import order par nirbhar karta hai — jaise base-button.module.css page.module.css se pehle aata hai kyunki <BaseButton> page.module.css se pehle import hua hai. Salah: CSS imports ko ek hi entry file tak rakho; global + Tailwind styles app root par import karo; zyada tar styling ke liye Tailwind ko preference do; jab utilities kaafi na hon tab CSS Modules; consistent naming (<name>.module.css); shared styles ko shared components me nikalo; import auto-sorters (ESLint sort-imports) band karo; chunking ko control karne ke liye cssChunking next.config option use karo.

Development banam production: dev (next dev) me CSS updates Fast Refresh ke saath turant lagu hote hain. Production (next build) me saari CSS kai minified, code-split .css files me concatenate hoti hai; har route ke liye minimal CSS. Production me JS disabled hone par bhi CSS load hoti hai, lekin dev me Fast Refresh ke liye JS chahiye. Dev me CSS ordering alag ho sakti hai — final order hamesha next build se verify karo.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Global CSS navigation par routes ke paar leak hoti hai (unload nahi hoti).
  • Import order = cascade order, isliye auto-sort kiye gaye imports styling tod dete hain.
  • Dev/prod ke beech CSS order ke antar.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
CSS Modules kyun exist karte hain (unique class names ke through scoping); Tailwind v4 setup (PostCSS plugin + @import 'tailwindcss'); global CSS ki navigation wali caveat; Next.js production me CSS ko chunk kaise karta hai.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/css
