Image Optimization

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Image Optimization. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Image Optimization — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — next/image ka <Image> <img> ko chaar faydon ke saath extend karta hai: size optimization (har device ke liye sahi size, WebP jaise modern formats); visual stability (layout shift / CLS ko automatic rokta hai); tez page loads (native lazy loading — sirf viewport me aane par load hota hai — plus optional blur-up placeholders); asset flexibility (on-demand resizing, remote images ke liye bhi).

%
tsx
import Image from 'next/image'
export default function Page() {
  return <Image src="" alt="" />
}
%

Local images: public/ ke neeche store karo; / se reference karo (jaise public/profile.png → /profile.png). String src ke liye width + height zaroori hain (ye aspect ratio set karte hain aur CLS rokte hain):

%
tsx
<Image src="/profile.png" alt="Picture of the author" width={500} height={500} />
%

Static imports (sabse best): Next.js intrinsic width, height aur blurDataURL automatic tay kar deta hai — inhe pass karne ki zaroorat nahi; blur-up ke liye placeholder="blur" jodo:

%
tsx
import ProfileImage from './profile.png'
<Image src={ProfileImage} alt="Picture of the author" />
%

Server Component me dynamic import (jab filename sirf runtime par pata chale): await import(`../content/blog/images/${imageFilename}`) width/height/blurDataURL ke saath image object return karta hai. Path me ek static prefix hona chahiye — usse match karne wali saari files bundle ho jati hain; external input directory se bahar nahi ja sakta. Path aliases (@/) bhi kaam karte hain.

Remote images: src ke liye URL string do; tumhe width, height aur optionally blurDataURL manually dena hoga (Next.js build par remote files ko inspect nahi kar sakta). Ya parent element ko fill karne ke liye fill prop use karo. Security: remote hosts ko next.config.js me images.remotePatterns se allow karo — jitna specific ho sake utna rakho:

%
ts
// next.config.ts
const config: NextConfig = {
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      {
        protocol: 'https',
        hostname: 's3.amazonaws.com',
        port: '',
        pathname: '/my-bucket/**',
        search: '',
      },
    ],
  },
}
%

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • remotePatterns ke bina remote images block ho jati hain.
  • Width/height ke bina string src error deta hai.
  • fill ke liye positioned parent chahiye.
  • Automatic blurDataURL sirf static imports se milta hai.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
<Image> woh kya karta hai jo <img> nahi karta (resizing, WebP, CLS prevention, lazy loading); width/height CLS kyun rokte hain; remotePatterns ek security allowlist ke roop me; static import banam string src ke trade-offs.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/images
Hissa 14 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Font Optimization

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Font Optimization. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Font Optimization — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — next/font: fonts ko automatic optimize karta hai aur external network requests ko hata deta hai (privacy + performance). Kisi bhi font file ke liye built-in self-hosting — optimally load hone wale web fonts, bina kisi layout shift ke. next/font/local ya next/font/google se import karo, options ke saath function ki tarah call karo, aur returned className apply karo. Fonts usi component tak scoped hote hain jisme use hue hain — poori app par lagana ho to Root Layout me jodo.

Google Fonts (auto self-hosted): fonts static assets ke roop me tumhare khud ke domain se serve hote hain — browser Google ko koi request nahi bhejta:

%
tsx
import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
const geist = Geist({ subsets: ['latin'] })
export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" className={geist.className}>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
%

Behtareen performance/flexibility ke liye variable fonts ko preference do. Non-variable fonts ko explicit weight chahiye:

%
tsx
import { Roboto } from 'next/font/google'
const roboto = Roboto({ weight: '400', subsets: ['latin'] })
%

Local fonts — next/font/local: src us file ke relative resolve hota hai jahan localFont call hua hai; fonts kahin bhi reh sakte hain (public/ me bhi ya app/fonts/ me colocated bhi):

%
tsx
import localFont from 'next/font/local'
const myFont = localFont({ src: './my-font.woff2' })
%

Ek family ke liye kai files — src ek array ke roop me, har file ke liye path/weight/style:

%
js
const roboto = localFont({
  src: [
    { path: './Roboto-Regular.woff2', weight: '400', style: 'normal' },
    { path: './Roboto-Italic.woff2', weight: '400', style: 'italic' },
    { path: './Roboto-Bold.woff2', weight: '700', style: 'normal' },
    { path: './Roboto-BoldItalic.woff2', weight: '700', style: 'italic' },
  ],
})
%

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • className asal me apply karna hota hai (sirf import karne se kuch nahi hota).
  • Fonts scoped hote hain — root layout bhool gaye to font sirf usi component ko milega.
  • weight ke bina non-variable Google fonts fail ho jate hain.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
self-hosting kyun mayne rakhta hai (koi Google requests nahi, privacy, koi render-blocking external CSS nahi); variable fonts banam weights; next/font layout shift kaise khatm karta hai (andar se font-display + size-adjust).
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fonts
Hissa 15 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Metadata and OG images

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Metadata and OG images. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Metadata and OG images — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — teen Metadata APIs: (1) static metadata object; (2) dynamic generateMetadata function; (3) special file conventions (favicons, OG images, robots, sitemap). Next.js relevant <head> tags automatic generate kar deta hai. metadata aur generateMetadata sirf Server Components me supported hain.

Default fields (hamesha jode jate hain): <meta charset="utf-8" /> aur <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />.

Static metadata: kisi static layout.js ya page.js se ek Metadata object export karo:

%
tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next'
export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'My Blog',
  description: '...',
}
%

Generated metadata: generateMetadata ko { params, searchParams } (dono Promises) + parent: ResolvingMetadata milta hai, aur ye data-dependent metadata fetch karta hai:

%
tsx
import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
type Props = {
  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
}
export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }: Props, parent: ResolvingMetadata): Promise<Metadata> {
  const slug = (await params).slug
  const post = await fetch(`https://api.vercel.app/blog/${slug}`).then((res) => res.json())
  return { title: post.title, description: post.description }
}
%

Streaming metadata: dynamically rendered pages ke liye, Next.js metadata ko alag se stream karta hai — generateMetadata ke resolve hote hi use HTML me inject kar deta hai, bina UI rendering ko block kiye — visual content pehle stream hota hai. Bots/crawlers ke liye disabled hai (Twitterbot, Slackbot, Bingbot wagera, User-Agent se detect hote hain) jinhe metadata <head> me chahiye; htmlLimitedBots config se customize/disable kiya ja sakta hai. Prerendered pages metadata stream nahi karte (wo build time par resolve hota hai).

Data requests ko memoize karna: generateMetadata aur page aksar ek hi data fetch karte hain — fetcher ko React ke cache() me wrap karo taaki wo ek hi baar execute ho:

%
ts
import { cache } from 'react'
export const getPost = cache(async (slug: string) => {
  const res = await db.query.posts.findFirst({ where: eq(posts.slug, slug) })
  return res
})
%

File-based metadata: favicon.ico, apple-icon.jpg, icon.jpg, opengraph-image.jpg, twitter-image.jpg, robots.txt, sitemap.xml — static files, ya code se programmatically generated.

Favicons: favicon.ico ko app folder ki root me jodo (code se bhi generate ho sakta hai).

Static OG images: app root me opengraph-image.jpg; per-route ke liye use aur deep rakho (jaise /blog ke liye blog/ ke andar). Zyada specific images folder structure me upar wali images par precedence leti hain. .jpeg, .png, .gif bhi supported hain.

Generated OG images — ImageResponse: jaise blog/[slug]/ ke andar opengraph-image.tsx, next/og ke ImageResponse ke saath JSX + CSS use karke; size (jaise 1200×630) aur contentType export karo:

%
tsx
import { ImageResponse } from 'next/og'
import { getPost } from '@/app/lib/data'
export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }
export const contentType = 'image/png'
export default async function Image({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const post = await getPost(slug)
  return new ImageResponse(
    (
      <div style={{ fontSize: 128, background: 'white', width: '100%', height: '100%', display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>
        {post.title}
      </div>
    )
  )
}
%

ImageResponse aam CSS support karta hai — flexbox, absolute positioning, custom fonts, text wrapping, centering, nested images. Andar se: @vercel/og, satori, resvg HTML/CSS ko PNG me badalte hain. Sirf flexbox + CSS ka ek subset — display: grid aur dusre advanced layouts kaam NAHI karenge. Examples: Vercel OG Playground.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Metadata APIs Client Components me kaam nahi kartin.
  • React.cache ke bina generateMetadata + page double-fetch karte hain.
  • ImageResponse me grid CSS chupchap fail ho jata hai.
  • Bots ko blocking (non-streamed) metadata milta hai.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
static banam generated metadata; streaming metadata aur bots ko usse bahar kyun rakha gaya hai; metadata aur page ke beech React.cache dedup; OG images ke liye file-convention precedence; ImageResponse ki CSS limitations.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images
Hissa 16 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Route Handlers

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Route Handlers. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Route Handlers — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: Web Request/Response APIs ka use karke kisi route ke liye custom request handlers banao. Sirf app directory ke andar available; Pages Router ke API Routes ka App Router equivalent — ek hi cheez ke liye dono ko ek saath mat use karo.

Convention: app ke andar ek route.js|ts file:

%
ts
// app/api/route.ts
export async function GET(request: Request) {}
%

Route Handlers page.js/layout.js ki tarah kahin bhi nest ho sakte hain, lekin page.js ke saath ek hi segment level par route.js nahi ho sakta (conflict — har route.js/page.js us route ke saare HTTP verbs ko le leta hai). Valid: app/page.js + app/api/route.js; invalid: app/page.js + app/route.js.

Supported HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS. Unsupported method → 405 Method Not Allowed.

Extended APIs: Next.js native Request/Response ko NextRequest / NextResponse se extend karta hai (advanced use cases ke liye helpers).

Caching (previous model): Route Handlers by default cached nahi hote; sirf GET opt-in kar sakta hai (dusre methods kabhi cached nahi hote, ek hi file me cached GET ke saath bhi nahi) — jaise export const dynamic = 'force-static':

%
ts
export const dynamic = 'force-static'
export async function GET() {
  const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY },
  })
  const data = await res.json()
  return Response.json({ data })
}
%

Cache Components ke saath: GET Route Handlers UI routes wala hi model follow karte hain — by default request time par chalte hain; jab wo uncached/runtime data access nahi karte to prerender ho jate hain; 'use cache' (kisi helper function me, handler body me directly nahi) uncached data ko static response me shamil kar deta hai, cacheLife ke hisaab se revalidate hokar. Prerendering ruk jati hai agar handler inme se kuch access kare: network requests, DB queries, async fs, request object ki properties (req.url, request.headers, request.cookies, request.body), runtime APIs (cookies(), headers(), connection()), ya non-deterministic operations (Math.random()).

%
tsx
// Cached example
import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
export async function GET() {
  const products = await getProducts()
  return Response.json(products)
}
async function getProducts() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')
  return await db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
}
%

Special Route Handlers: sitemap.ts, opengraph-image.tsx, icon.tsx aur dusri metadata files by default static rehti hain, jab tak wo request-time APIs ya dynamic config use na karein.

Route resolution: route sabse low-level routing primitive hai — ye page ki tarah layouts ya client-side navigations me participate nahi karta.

Route Context Helper (TS): globally available RouteContext context param ko type karta hai (next dev/next build/next typegen par generate hota hai):

%
ts
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) {
  const { id } = await ctx.params
  return Response.json({ id })
}
%

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Ek hi segment me route.js + page.js = conflict.
  • Sirf GET cacheable hai.
  • 'use cache' handler body me directly nahi ja sakta.
  • Non-GET methods kabhi cached nahi hote.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
Route Handlers banam API Routes; ek segment me page.js + route.js kyun nahi reh sakte; har method ke caching rules; Cache Components ke prerendering triggers; RouteContext typing.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers
Hissa 17 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Proxy

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Proxy. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Proxy — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — Next.js 16 me naam badla: Middleware ko ab Proxy kehte hain (functionality wahi hai, naam uske maksad ko behtar darshata hai). Proxy kisi request ke complete hone se pehle code chalata hai; incoming request ke aadhar par tum rewrite kar sakte ho, redirect kar sakte ho, request/response headers modify kar sakte ho, ya directly respond kar sakte ho.

Use cases: saare/kuch pages ke liye headers modify karna; A/B tests/experiments ke liye dusre pages par rewrite karna; request properties ke aadhar par programmatic redirects. Simple redirects ke liye pehle next.config.ts ki redirects config ko preference do — Proxy tab use karo jab tumhe request data ya complex logic chahiye ho.

Limitations (zaroori): Proxy slow data fetching ke liye nahi hai; optimistic checks (jaise permission-based redirects) ke liye achha hai, lekin poora session-management/authorization solution nahi hai. Proxy me 'use cache' aur 'use server' directives ka koi asar nahi hota (koi directive transforms nahi). Proxy me fetch ke options cache, next.revalidate, next.tags responses ko cache nahi karte — cached data ko kisi external cache/data store se reuse karo, ya kaam ko Server Component/Route Handler me le jao.

Convention: har project me ek hi proxy.ts (ya .js) file, project root me ya src ke andar (pages/app ke level par). Sirf ek hi file supported hai — logic ko modules me organize karke us ek proxy.ts me import karo (saaf management, koi conflicting layers nahi).

Example:

%
ts
// proxy.ts
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}
// Alternatively: export default function proxy(request: NextRequest) { ... }

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
%

matcher config Proxy ko specific paths tak filter karta hai (path matching ke liye Matcher docs dekho).

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Sirf ek hi proxy file hoti hai.
  • Andar koi caching/directives kaam nahi karte.
  • Yahan auth/session logic ya slow fetches mat rakho.
  • Simple redirects Proxy me nahi, config me belong karte hain.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
Middleware ka naam Proxy kyun rakha gaya; Proxy kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi; matcher; Proxy me auth checks sirf "optimistic" kyun hote hain (asli authorization Server Components/Route Handlers/Server Actions me honi chahiye).
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/proxy
Hissa 18 / 471 · App Router · Getting Started

Deploying

App RouterGetting Started

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Getting Started hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Deploying. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Deploying — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — chaar deployment options:

OptionFeature support
Node.js serversab
Docker containersab
Static exportlimited
Adaptersalag-alag (verified adapters test suite chalate hain)

Node.js server: Node.js support karne wale kisi bhi provider par deploy karo. package.json me "build" aur "start" scripts chahiye; npm run build chalao, phir npm run start. Saare Next.js features support karta hai; zaroorat padne par custom server par eject bhi kar sakte ho. Self-hosting configuration guide infrastructure setup cover karti hai. Templates: Flightcontrol, Railway, Replit, Hostinger.

Docker: Docker support karne wala koi bhi provider (Kubernetes orchestrators samet). Best practices ke liye Docker ke official Next.js/React.js guides follow karo. Saare features support karta hai. Dev note: behtar performance ke liye Mac/Windows par development ke dauran Docker ke bajay local dev (npm run dev) use karo. Templates: Docker Standalone Output (output: "standalone" — sirf zaroori runtime files/deps wali minimal production image), Docker Export Output (output: "export" — poori tarah static, lightweight container ya static hosting se serve), Docker Multi-Environment (dev/staging/prod ke liye alag configs, alag env vars ke saath). Provider guides: DigitalOcean, Fly.io, Google Cloud Run, Render, SST.

Static export: ek static site ya SPA ke roop me shuru karo, baad me chaaho to server features par upgrade kar lo. Kisi bhi static web server (AWS S3, Nginx, Apache) par host karo. Server mangne wale features support nahi karta. Template: GitHub Pages.

Adapters: Deployment Adapter API (adapterPath config) platforms ko build/deploy customize karne deti hai. Verified adapters (open source, poori Next.js compatibility test suite chalate hain, Next.js GitHub org ke under hosted hain, major releases se pehle coordinated testing hoti hai): Vercel, Bun. Cloudflare aur Netlify verified adapters par kaam kar rahe hain; tab tak wo apni khud ki integrations dete hain (unverified, feature support alag ho sakta hai): Appwrite Sites, AWS Amplify Hosting, Cloudflare, Deno Deploy, Firebase App Hosting, Netlify.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Static export server features ko chupchap hata deta hai — use chunne se pehle unsupported-features list check karo.
  • Unverified platform integrations features par peeche reh sakti hain.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
chaar options aur unka feature support; output: "standalone" banam output: "export"; "verified adapter" ka matlab kya hai.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — latest version: upgrade command use karo:

%
bash
npx next upgrade        # npm
pnpm next upgrade
yarn next upgrade
bunx next upgrade
%

Next.js 16.1.0 se pehle ke versions upgrade command support nahi karte — iske bajay codemod use karo: npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest. Agent-driven upgrade: npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest ("Upgrade with a coding agent" guide me policies/reminders dekho).

Manual upgrade: latest Next.js + React install karo:

%
bash
npm i next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest eslint-config-next@latest
%

Canary version: pehle latest stable par jao aur confirm karo ki sab kaam kar raha hai, phir:

%
bash
npm i next@canary
%

Abhi canary me maujud features (docs ke time par): Authentication — forbidden, unauthorized functions; forbidden.js, unauthorized.js files; authInterrupts config.

Version guides: Version 16 (15→16), Version 15 (14→15), Version 14 (13→14) — har ek me gehrai se upgrade instructions.

Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
next upgrade banam codemod (16.1.0 ki cutoff); canary se pehle latest stable par kyun jayein; canary = pre-release features (yahan: auth interrupts).

Hissa 21 / 471 · App Router · Guides

Adopting Partial Prefetching

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Adopting Partial Prefetching. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Adopting Partial Prefetching — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: Partial Prefetching badal deta hai ki ek <Link> Cache Components wale route ke liye kya download karta hai. Iske enabled hone par, <Link> route ka App Shell prefetch karta hai — static content + woh cached content jo URL par nirbhar nahi karta. Next.js har route ke liye ek App Shell banata hai aur use us route ke har link ke liye reuse karta hai (pehle har link alag se prefetch hota tha). App Shell se zyada prefetch karna ho to link <Link prefetch={true}> se per-link prefetching me opt-in karta hai, jo params, searchParams ya poore URL par nirbhar cached URL-specific content ko resolve karta hai. Next.js development me instant navigation insights dikhata hai jo badle jane wale link/route ka naam batate hain. Partial Prefetching sirf tab kaam karta hai jab cacheComponents enabled ho.

Recommended raasta — adoption skill: npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption, phir agent ko prompt do: "Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill." Skill <Link prefetch={true}> calls ko review karta hai, preserve ki jane wali prefetched UI ko instant() tests se capture karta hai (jab production test rig maujud ho), flag enable karta hai, aur har route ko check karta hai.

Haath se apnao (4 steps): (1) existing full prefetches ko review karo, tay karo ki har destination ka kaunsa hissa prefetch hota rehna chahiye (regression coverage ke liye instant() tests use karo); (2) partialPrefetching enable karo — ya global flag band rakhkar incrementally apnao ("dynamic data during prefetching" insight un destinations ko pehchanta hai jo ab bhi legacy full prefetch use kar rahe hain); (3) URL data ko Suspense ke peeche le jao ("URL data outside of Suspense" insight ko resolve karke); (4) chaaho to wahan URL data prefetch karo jahan navigation ke baad streaming kaafi na ho. Dono insights sirf development me aate hain, build ko kabhi block nahi karte, aur dev overlay me fix cards ke saath dikhte hain. Taiyar nahi ho? Page/layout se instant = false export karke instant-navigation validation se opt out kar do aur baad me wapas aao.

Enable karna:

%
ts
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}
%

Enable karne ke baad, default/"auto"/true links destination ka App Shell prefetch karte hain; prefetch={true} cached URL-specific content bhi resolve kar sakta hai, lekin legacy full prefetch wala uncached dynamic content ab isme shamil nahi hota. Naye projects bina audit ke enable kar sakte hain (koi legacy prefetches nahi). Warning: partialPrefetching value ke bina cacheComponents warning log karta hai; purana behaviour migration ke dauran rakhna ho tabhi false set karo. Agli major release me dono har jagah enabled honge; options hat jayenge.

<Link> ke liye kya badalta hai:

<Link> propPehlePartial Prefetching ke baad
<Link href="/x">cached page render prefetch hota tha/x ka shared App Shell prefetch hota hai
<Link href="/x" prefetch>cached page render aur koi bhi dynamic content prefetch hota thaApp Shell + per-link prefetching se cached URL-specific content
<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>disabledkoi badlav nahi — ab bhi disabled

App Shell ek route ke har link ke beech shared hota hai, dynamic params chahe jo hon — isliye ek hi destination ke kai <Link> kaam ko kai guna nahi badhate.

Existing full prefetches ko migrate karna: pehle, effective prefetch={true} wala <Link> (bare prefetch prop aur true par resolve hone wale wrapper/conditional props samet) poore destination ko, uncached dynamic content samet, prefetch karta tha. Default "auto" aur false legacy full prefetch use nahi karte. Ek legacy full prefetch navigation ki zaroorat se zyada UI shamil kar sakta hai — primary top-of-page content navigation se pehle available hona chahiye; secondary/bar-bar badalne wala content baad me stream ho sakta hai.

Key antar: cookies()/headers() kisi prefetch ko URL se nahi jodte (ye per session badalte hain, per link nahi) — App Shell me session content phir bhi rehta hai. Sirf params aur searchParams URL data hain (per link badalte hain, shared App Shell me nahi ho sakte).

Prefetched UI ko tests se verify karo — instant(): Playwright test jo us UI ko capture karta hai jo existing full prefetch se available rehni chahiye; exact source link ko test karo (ek hi destination ke alag links ki prefetch settings alag ho sakti hain). Baseline ko partialPrefetching disabled karke production build par chalao (automatic prefetching next dev me nahi chalti), apnane ke baad dobara chalao; agar fail ho, to UI ab prefetch nahi ho rahi — reusable data/subtree ko cache karo, aur passing test ko regression coverage ke roop me rakho:

%
ts
import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products')
  await instant(page, async () => {
    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
    await link.click()
    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })).toBeVisible()
    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
  })
})
%

Migration decision table:

DestinationSalah
poori tarah static, ya content pehle se cachedfaltu prefetch={true} hata do
uncached content jo tum click se pehle rakha chahte house use cache se cache karo, phir prefetch={true} hata do
cookies()/headers() par nirbhar contentlookup ko session value ke peeche cache karo, phir prefetch={true} hata do
URL data padhta hai, ya us par nirbhar cached contentprefetch={true} rakho taaki click se pehle resolve ho
real-time content, har request par fresh rehna chahiyeprefetch={true} hata do, use stream-in hone do

Udaharan: static/cached — <Link href="/about" prefetch={true}> → <Link href="/about">. Uncached — fetch ko ek 'use cache' helper (getProducts()) me wrap karo, phir App Shell use le jata hai. Session — cookie ko cached function ke bahar padho, value ko andar pass karo ('use cache' ke saath getTopics(team)). Note: App Shell woh cached content le jata hai jiska stale time kam se kam 5 minute ho (default profile aur seconds ke alawa har preset); usse chhoti umar wala content navigation ke baad stream hota hai.

Incrementally apnana: prefetch = 'partial' global flag ko ek route tak scoped kar deta hai — global flag band ho to har destination ko apne hisaab se apnao/deploy karo. Koi destination opt-in kare, usse pehle prefetch={true} legacy full prefetch karta hai; dev me aise link se navigate karne par fixes ke saath "dynamic data during prefetching" insight dikhta hai: opt in karo (page/layout me export const prefetch = 'partial') ya default prefetch use karo. Steps: (1) intended prefetched UI ko preserve karo, uske prefetch={true} links ko patterns ke hisaab se update karo; uske page/layout me export const prefetch = 'partial' jodo (us route ke har link ke liye insight saaf ho jata hai). Dhyaan do: agar page/layout pehle se next/cache se prefetch() call karta hai, to use dusre naam se import karo (import { prefetch as prefetchStage }) taaki prefetch export se takraye na. (2) Deploy karo. (3) Dohrao, phir global flag enable karo. Cleanup: npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app har page/layout se export const prefetch = 'partial' hata deta hai (src/ projects ke liye ./src/app use karo; galat path fail hone ke bajay 0 ok report karta hai — file count check karo). Codemod sirf 'partial' hatata hai, jaise prefetch = 'force-disabled' ko chhod deta hai.

URL data ko Suspense ke peeche le jao: flag on hone par, Next.js dev me har App Shell ko validate karta hai. params/searchParams ko <Suspense> ke bahar padhna shell ko ek URL se bandh deta hai → "URL data outside of Suspense" insight, fixes ke saath: Suspense me wrap karo, ya export const instant = false se block karo. Fix: URL-independent hisse boundary ke bahar rakho; read ko ek child me le jao jo <Suspense> me wrapped ho — params promise ko bina await kiye neeche pass karo:

%
tsx
// Before — awaiting params at top ties App Shell to one URL
export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const product = await getProduct(slug)
  return (
    <ProductLayout>
      <Details product={product} />
    </ProductLayout>
  )
}
// After
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
  return (
    <ProductLayout>
      <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
        <ProductDetails params={params} />
      </Suspense>
    </ProductLayout>
  )
}
// product-details.tsx — awaits inside the boundary
export async function ProductDetails({ params }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const product = await getProduct(slug)
  return <Details product={product} />
}
%

Note: generateMetadata ke andar params/searchParams read ek alag insight ke roop me aata hai ("URL data in generateMetadata()").

URL data ko prefetch karna: URL-dependent content shared App Shell me nahi ho sakta — wo navigation ke baad stream hota hai. Per-link prefetching (prefetch={true}) use click se pehle resolve kar deta hai, jiski keemat hai har prefetchable link par ek server invocation. Prefetch time par resolvable banane ke liye, use read ke peeche 'use cache' se cache karo (jaise search page: boundary ke andar searchParams ko await karne ke baad call hone wala 'use cache' wala getResults(query)).

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • instant() tests sirf production builds par kaam karte hain (dev me auto-prefetch nahi hota).
  • prefetch export ka naam prefetch() function import se takrata hai.
  • Chhota stale (< 5 min) wala cached content App Shell me nahi jayega.
  • Insights sirf dev me hain aur builds ko kabhi block nahi karte.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
App Shell banam full prefetch; har route ke liye ek App Shell sasta kyun hai; URL data banam session data ka antar; incremental adoption ka raasta (per-route prefetch = 'partial' + codemod cleanup); prefetch={true} kab rakhein.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching
Hissa 22 / 471 · App Router · Guides

How Next.js supports AI coding agents

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How Next.js supports AI coding agents. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How Next.js supports AI coding agents — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — samasya: AI coding agents us training data par bharosa kar sakte hain jo installed Next.js version se purana ho. Next.js version-matched docs, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills aur optional agent feedback deta hai. Results: nextjs.org/evals par Next.js agent evaluations. Background: Next.js 16.2 + 16.3 AI tooling blog posts.

Version-matched documentation (16.2+): Installed version se match karne wale docs package ke andar node_modules/next/dist/docs/ par ship hote hain, docs site structure ko mirror karte hue (01-app/01-getting-started/, 02-guides/, 03-api-reference/, 02-pages/, 03-architecture/, index.mdx). Agents bina network requests ke current APIs paate hain. Next.js upgrade karne se bundled docs update ho jate hain. Project root par AGENTS.md me managed instructions (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot session start par padhte hain) agents ko bundled docs ki taraf point karte hain. create-next-app naye projects ke liye agent files banata hai; next dev maujooda projects ke liye managed instructions banata/update karta hai jab ye ek coding agent detect karta hai. Managed block (<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules --> … <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->) kehta hai: 'Ye wo Next.js NAHI hai jise tum jante ho — is version me breaking changes hain… koi bhi code likhne se pehle node_modules/next/dist/docs/ me relevant guide padho. Deprecation notices par dhyaan do.' Next.js sirf markers ke beech ki content update karta hai, baaki AGENTS.md preserve rakhta hai. Research: AGENTS.md + bundled docs = evals me 100% pass rate, Skill-based approaches ke liye 79% tak ke mukable. Managed instructions 16.3+ me default roop se enabled hain (agentRules se configure/disable). Version support: 16.3+ = bundled docs + auto instructions; 16.2 = bundled docs, koi auto instructions nahi; 16.1 aur pehle = koi bundled docs nahi — legacy npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md ek version-matched copy .next-docs/ me download karta hai aur use AGENTS.md me index karta hai.

Network par Docs: nextjs.org/docs ke har page ka ek plain Markdown version uske .md URL par hai; Accept: text/markdown bhejne wale clients ko Markdown milta hai. /docs/messages ke tahat per-error pages shamil hain (bundled nahi). /docs/llms.txt par index aur single-file /docs/llms-full.txt llms.txt convention follow karte hain.

Automatic agent feedback (experimental, default roop se off, Telemetry chahiye, CI me kabhi nahi chalta): Agents request ke dauraan anonymized facts ko feedback candidates ke roop me rakhte hain (crashes/hangs/OOM/slowness; galat behavior/output/errors/diagnostics; missing/unclear/conflicting docs; unexpected CLI/codemod/Skill/upgrade behavior + non-obvious workarounds). Routine debugging feedback nahi hai. Final response se pehle, ek reporting pass npx --no-install next internal agent-feedback-instructions chalata hai; har qualifying report default browser me ek alag review form me khulti hai. Kholne se pehle, agent report ko anonymize karta hai (customer/project details ko generic descriptions se badal kar, source code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, PII hata kar). Jab tak tum 'Send feedback' select nahi karte, kuch bheja nahi jata. experimental.agentFeedback → agentFeedback config se enable hota hai; next dev AGENTS.md me managed feedback block likhta hai.

Agent-guided upgrades: npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest — available upgrade ke liye check karta hai, version-matched migration guides ikatthe karta hai, kaam ek coding agent ko deta hai jo changes apply karta hai aur app verify karta hai. Experimental agentUpgrade option next dev / next build ke dauraan default roop se security upgrade reminders dikhata hai.

Runtime visibility: Agents ko framework + browser state chahiye. next dev browser console errors/warnings ko terminal par forward karta hai (logging.browserToTerminal), isliye agent ke padhe output me client failures aate hain. next dev PID/port/URL ko .next/dev/lock me likhta hai; next dev dobara chalane par maujooda server ka URL + PID + stop command print hota hai (jab mumkin ho maujooda server ke saath jaari rakho). Framework view: /_next/mcp par Next.js MCP server routes, server logs, compilation issues expose karta hai (get_compilation_issues, compile_route — compilation check karne ke liye full next build ki zaroorat nahi). Browser view: next-dev-loop skill + agent-browser CLI DOM, console, network, Web Vitals ko structured text ke roop me expose karte hain, React DevTools ke saath (component tree, pending Suspense boundaries).

Errors ke liye built-in guidance: Cache Components enabled hone par, ek blocking error alag trade-offs wale labeled fixes pesh karta hai; dev overlay ek Copy prompt button jodta hai jo chosen fix ko paste-ready prompt me pack karta hai (matching error page padho, canonical pattern apply karo, runtime par verify karo). Wahi menu next dev terminal aur next build output me print hota hai (CI logs padhne wale agents bhi use dekhte hain). Example: Route "/products/[slug]": Next.js encountered uncached data during prerendering → fixes: [stream] <Suspense fallback>; [cache] "use cache" (connection() ke liye nahi); [block] export const instant = false. 'Learn more' links /docs/messages ke tahat per-error pages par jate hain (canonical patterns, trade-offs, gotchas). next dev validation errors source-mapped stacks ke saath dikhata hai; production builds server code minify karte hain aur ek route fail hone ke baad ruk jate hain — server source maps + dusre routes check jaari rakhne ke liye next build --debug-prerender use karo.

Multi-step workflows ke liye Skills: Framework knowledge bundled docs se aata hai, Skills se nahi (benchmarks: always-available context on-demand retrieval ko haraata hai). Skills workflows cover karti hain: next-dev-loop (runtime foundation: MCP + browser ke through inspect/edit/verify cycle — npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-dev-loop); next-bundle-optimizer (v16.4.0; bade client bundles ke liye Turbopack bundle analyzer; audit-only report mode ya fix mode); next-cache-components-adoption (Cache Components par migrate: flag on → non-prerenderable routes dhoondho → user checkpoints ke saath ek feature ek baar me fix karo → dev + build se verify karo; PR series ya single branch); next-cache-components-optimizer (ek route ke static shell ko badhao: failing instant() test likho → pass hone tak refactor karo → test ko regression coverage ke roop me commit karo); next-partial-prefetching-adoption (<Link prefetch={true}> audit karo, UI ko instant() tests me capture karo, flag enable karo, insights resolve karo; Cache Components + production-like build chahiye); next-partial-prefetching-optimizer (per-navigation prefetch contracts → instant() tests → optimizing-prefetching patterns). Skills ka source dekho: github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills; skills.sh/vercel/next.js.

Gadbad (gotchas): Bundled docs sirf 16.2+ me; AGENTS.md managed block next dev dwara dobara joda jata hai (tree saaf rakhne ke liye use commit karo); feedback ke liye Telemetry chahiye aur explicit 'Send feedback' ke bina kabhi bheja nahi jata; instant() tests ko production builds chahiye.

Interview points: Bundled version-matched docs training data ko kyun harate hain (100% vs 79% evals); AGENTS.md managed-block mechanism; runtime visibility (MCP server + browser tools); structured error guidance aur Copy prompt; Skills workflows ke liye hain, framework knowledge ke liye nahi.

Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/ai-agents
Hissa 23 / 471 · App Router · Guides

How to add analytics to your Next.js application

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How to add analytics to your Next.js application. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How to add analytics to your Next.js application — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: Next.js ne measuring/reporting performance metric ke liye built-in support kiya hai. do routes: useReportWebVitals hook (apne aap ko riporting prabndhit karein) ya Vercel ke prabndhit Analytics/Speed insights serve (automatic sangrah + view).

Client instrumentation — instrumentation-client.js|ts: apne app ke frontend code ko executed karne ke liye before chalata hai. global vishleshan, error traiking, performance nigrani setup ke liye aadarsha. app root mein banaein:

js
// instrumentation-client.js
console.log('Analytics initialized')
window.addEventListener('error', (event) => {
  reportError(event.error)
})

Build your own — useReportWebVitals: ka upyog Client Component mein kiya jana chahiye - ek alag 'use client' file banayein aur ise client boundary ko chhota rakhne ke liye root layout mein import karein:

jsx
// app/_components/web-vitals.js
'use client'
import { useReportWebVitals } from 'next/web-vitals'
export function WebVitals() {
  useReportWebVitals((metric) => {
    console.log(metric)
  })
}
// app/layout.js
import { WebVitals } from './_components/web-vitals'
export default function Layout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        <WebVitals />
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}

Web Vitals ne report ki: TTFB (First Byte ke liye samay), FCP (First Contentful Paint), LCP (Largest Contentful Paint), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift), INP (Next Paint ke liye intrekshan). pratyek ko ek svich mein metric.name ke madhyam se sambhal lein.

external pranaliyon ke liye Sending parinam: metric JSON ko kisi bhi endpoint par bhejein; fetch({ keepalive: true }) fallback ke sath navigator.sendBeacon() ko pasand karein:

js
useReportWebVitals((metric) => {
  const body = JSON.stringify(metric)
  const url = 'https://example.com/analytics'
  if (navigator.sendBeacon) {
    navigator.sendBeacon(url, body)
  } else {
    fetch(url, { body, method: 'POST', keepalive: true })
  }
})

Google Analytics: distributions/percentiles banane ke liye event_label ke roop mein metric.id (Unique per page load) ka upyog karein; window.gtag('event', metric.name, { value: Math.round(metric.name === 'CLS'? metric.value * 1000: metric.value), event_label: metric.id, non_interaction: true }) (values integer hona chahiye); non_interaction: true uchhal dar ko affected karne se rokta hai.

Dhyaan Do: ek Server Component error mein useReportWebVitals - ise 'use client' leaf mein alag karein; sendBeacon hamesha upalabdh nahi hai - prapt patan ko rokein.

Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
panch Web Vitals aur kya pratyek upaay; instrumentation-client samay (frontend code se pahle); kyon vishleshan ke liye sendBeacon (survives page utaranaa).
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/analytics
Hissa 24 / 471 · App Router · Guides

How to implement authentication in Next.js

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How to implement authentication in Next.js. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How to implement authentication in Next.js — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Server Components, Layouts — caution, Pages, Leaf components, Server Actions, Route Handlers. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts — teen concepts: (1) Authentication — identity verify karna (username/password); (2) Session Management — requests ke paar auth state ko track karna; (3) Authorization — tay karna ki user kin routes/data ko access kar sakta hai. Udaharan educational username/password auth ke hain; production ke liye docs ek auth library ki sifarish karte hain (built-in auth, sessions, authorization, social logins, MFA, RBAC). Cache Components enabled hon to session padhna + per-user caching khaas rules follow karte hain (Authentication with Cache Components guide dekho).

Signup/login — 3 steps:

1. Credentials capture karo: <form action={signup}> ek Server Action ko invoke karta hai (secure — hamesha server par chalta hai). Fields: name, email, password.

2. Server par validate karo: Server Action me Zod (ya Valibot/Yup) use karo; invalid fields par jaldi return karo taaki faltu provider/DB calls bachein. Udaharan schema: name min 2 chars; email valid; password min 8 chars + kam se kam ek letter, ek number, ek special character. Errors ko useActionState se dikhao (state ka shape { errors?: { name?: string[]; email?: string[]; password?: string[] }, message?: string }, validatedFields.error.flatten().fieldErrors se flattened). React 19 ka useFormStatus data, method, action keys jodta hai (React 19 se pehle sirf pending). Mutate karne se pehle hamesha authorization check karo.

3. User banao / credentials check karo: password ko store karne se pehle hash karo (bcrypt.hash(password, 10)), DB me daalo, phir ek session banao + redirect karo. Tip: behtar UX ke liye duplicate emails/usernames ko jaldi check karo (typing/blur par, use-debounce se debounced).

Session management — do tarah ke:

1. Stateless sessions: session data/token browser cookies me; cookie har request ke saath bheji jati hai; server verify karta hai. Saral hai, galat tareeke se kiya to kam secure.

2. Database sessions: session data DB me; browser ko sirf encrypted session ID milta hai. Zyada secure, zyada complex/resource-heavy. Recommended libraries: iron-session, jose.

Stateless session ke steps: (a) ek secret key generate karo (openssl rand -base64 32) → SESSION_SECRET env var ke roop me store karo. (b) jose se encrypt/decrypt karo (SignJWT/jwtVerify, HS256, 7-day expiry) + logic ko server-side rakhne ke liye server-only. Payload = minimum unique user data (user ID, role) — kabhi PII (phone, email, credit card) ya passwords nahi. (c) Next.js cookies() API se recommended options ke saath cookies set karo: httpOnly: true (koi JS access nahi), secure: true (sirf https), sameSite: 'lax', expires/maxAge, path: '/'.

%
ts
// app/lib/session.ts
import 'server-only'
import { SignJWT, jwtVerify } from 'jose'
const secretKey = process.env.SESSION_SECRET
const encodedKey = new TextEncoder().encode(secretKey)
export async function encrypt(payload: SessionPayload) {
  return new SignJWT(payload)
    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' })
    .setIssuedAt()
    .setExpirationTime('7d')
    .sign(encodedKey)
}
export async function decrypt(session: string | undefined = '') {
  try {
    const { payload } = await jwtVerify(session, encodedKey, { algorithms: ['HS256'] })
    return payload
  } catch (error) {
    console.log('Failed to verify session')
  }
}
export async function createSession(userId: string) {
  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
  const session = await encrypt({ userId, expiresAt })
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  cookieStore.set('session', session, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, expires: expiresAt, sameSite: 'lax', path: '/' })
}
%

(d) Refresh: updateSession() user ke wapas aane par nayi 7-day expiry ke saath cookie dobara issue karta hai (ya library support kare to refresh tokens use karo). (e) Delete: deleteSession() → cookieStore.delete('session'); logout action ise call karke phir redirect('/login') karta hai. Client tampering rokne ke liye cookies server par hi set honi chahiye.

Database sessions: (1) DB me sessions table; (2) insert/update/delete logic; (3) session ID ko browser cookie me store karne se pehle encrypt karo, DB + cookie ko sync rakho (Proxy me optimistic auth checks ke liye recommended). createSession(id): row insert karo → sessionId lo → { sessionId, expiresAt } encrypt karo → unhi options ke saath cookie set karo. Fayde: last login track karna, active devices, saare devices se log out. Tip: session lifetime ke liye server caching jodo; queries kam karne ke liye data requests ko combine karo.

Authorization — do tarah ke checks:

1. Optimistic: cookie me maujud session data use karta hai — tez (UI show/hide, redirects). Proxy + static routes ke liye achha (jaise paywalled content).

2. Secure: database me maujud session data use karta hai — sensitive data/actions ke liye. Dono ko ek Data Access Layer (DAL) + DTOs use karne chahiye, optimistic checks ke liye optionally Proxy ke saath.

Proxy se optimistic checks (optional): Proxy har route par chalta hai, prefetched routes samet — sirf cookie se session padho (performance ke liye koi DB checks nahi). Udaharan: protectedRoutes = ['/dashboard'], publicRoutes = ['/login', '/signup', '/']; cookie session decrypt karo; unauthenticated ko /login par redirect karo; authenticated ko public routes se /dashboard par redirect karo; matcher: ['/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|.*\\.png$).*)']. Tips: req.cookies.get('session')?.value Proxy me bhi kaam karta hai; Proxy Node.js runtime use karta hai — library compatibility check karo; matcher routes ko scope kar sakta hai, lekin auth ke liye salah hai ki Proxy saare routes par chale. Proxy tumhari ekmatra defense nahi honi chahiye — zyada tar checks data source ke kareeb (DAL me) hone chahiye.

Data Access Layer (DAL): data + authorization ko centralized rakho. verifySession() (ek render pass ke dauran React ke cache se memoized) cookie ko decrypt karta hai, userId na ho to /login par redirect karta hai, aur { isAuth: true, userId } return karta hai:

%
ts
// app/lib/dal.ts
import 'server-only'
import { cache } from 'react'
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
import { decrypt } from '@/app/lib/session'
export const verifySession = cache(async () => {
  const cookie = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
  const session = await decrypt(cookie)
  if (!session?.userId) {
    redirect('/login')
  }
  return { isAuth: true, userId: session.userId }
})
%

Note: React ka cache sirf ek render pass ke andar dedupe karta hai — Server Actions aur Route Handlers kisi render pass ka hissa nahi hote, isliye wahan wrapper kuch nahi karta aur har call function ko chalati hai. getUser() verifySession() + explicit column selection use karta hai (sirf zaroori columns, kabhi poore user objects nahi). DAL request-time data ko protect karta hai; static routes (build time par fetch hua data, jo users ke beech shared hota hai) ke liye Proxy use karo. Secure checks ke liye, session ID ko DB se compare karo. Related requests ko ek class me consolidate karo jo methods se pehle verifySession() chalaye.

DTOs: sirf zaroori data return karo; agar tum shape ko control nahi kar sakte, to field-level exposure rules use karo (canSeeUsername, canSeePhoneNumber(viewer, team) → admin ya same team). Patterns: toJSON(), individual functions, ya classes.

Kahan check karein:

  • Server Components: role-based rendering (admin → <AdminDashboard />, user → <UserDashboard />, warna redirect('/login')).
  • Layouts — savdhaan: layouts navigation par dobara render nahi hote (Partial Rendering), isliye wahan ke session checks har route change par nahi chalte. Ek layout ye bhi control nahi karta ki route ka baaki hissa render hoga ya nahi — segments/parallel slots router ke dwara render hote hain aur RSC Payload me aa jate hain, chahe layout unhe chhupa de. Checks data source/component ke kareeb karo. Jaise layout me getUser() fetch karo (nav avatar ke liye), lekin auth check getUser() ke andar wale DAL ko karne do. Layout me cookies()/headers()/DAL par top-level await pehle streamed chunk ko delay karta hai aur {children} ko rok deta hai — agar shell ke sirf ek hisse ko session data chahiye (user menu), to await ko <Suspense> me wrapped ek nested Server Component me le jao. Client Components DAL import nahi kar sakte — parent Server Component me verifySession()/getUser() chalao, data props ya context provider se pass karo; sensitive session fields ko client tak pahunchne se rokne ke liye taintUniqueValue use karo.
  • Pages: verifySession(), phir user-specific data fetch karo.
  • Leaf components: verifySession() + role check, non-admins ke liye return null (jaise <AdminActions>). Warning: layout/top-level component me return null authorization mechanism ke roop me recommended nahi hai — Next.js ke kai entry points hain; ye nested segments ya Server Actions tak access nahi rokega. Har Server Action ko apna authorization check khud karna hoga.
  • Server Actions: inhe public API endpoints ki tarah treat karo — verifySession(), role check karo, unauthorized ho to jaldi return karo.
  • Route Handlers: two-tier check — session nahi → 401; session hai lekin admin nahi → 403.

Auth libraries: Auth0, Better Auth, Clerk, Descope, Kinde, Logto, NextAuth.js (Auth.js), Ory, Stack Auth, Supabase, Stytch, WorkOS. Session libs: Iron Session, Jose. Aage padhne ke liye: "How to think about security in Next.js", XSS/CSRF guides, The Copenhagen Book.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • JWT payload me kabhi PII mat rakho.
  • Sirf Proxy par kabhi bharosa mat karo.
  • Security ke liye return null wali UI-hiding par kabhi bharosa mat karo.
  • Layouts navigation par sessions dobara check nahi karte.
  • cache() Server Actions/Route Handlers me dedupe nahi karta.
  • Cookies server-side hi set honi chahiye.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
auth banam session banam authorization; stateless banam database sessions; optimistic banam secure checks; DAL + DTO pattern aur ye kyun; Proxy checks sirf optimistic kyun hote hain; layouts auth checks ke liye galat jagah kyun hain; Route Handlers me 401 banam 403.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication
Hissa 25 / 471 · App Router · Guides

How to implement authentication with Cache Components

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How to implement authentication with Cache Components. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How to implement authentication with Cache Components — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: Cache Components enabled hon to session read request time par hota hai, isliye wo static shell me prerender nahi ho sakta. Iske bajay authenticated UI ek <Suspense> boundary ke peeche stream-in hoti hai, aur session se derived data phir bhi cache ho sakta hai. Udaharan iron-session (encrypted cookie sessions) use karte hain; patterns kisi bhi session/auth library par lagu hote hain. Runnable example: with-iron-session-cache-components. Prerequisite: next.config.ts me cacheComponents: true. Ye maan kar chalta hai ki login par session pehle se set hai; fundamentals Authentication aur Data Security guides me hain.

Migrate karna: instant-navigation validation har us route ko flag karta hai jo session padhta hai. Ship karne se pehle sabko theek karna zaroori nahi — page/layout par export const instant = false set karke server par blocking rakho, phir patterns ko ek-ek route karke apnao (Migrating to Cache Components dekho).

Step 1 — Current user ko padho: session cookie padho, user ko lookup karo. Hamesha <Suspense> ke peeche; har navigation par stream hota hai. Ek cache lifetime framework ko us content ko pehle se prefetch karne deta hai — lekin plain 'use cache' / 'use cache: remote' cookies() ko call nahi kar sakte, aur tum value ko extract-karke-pass bhi nahi kar sakte: session helper cookie ko apne code ke deep andar padhta hai (bahar nikalne ke liye kuch hai hi nahi), aur validation token ki expiry ko current time se compare karta hai (iron-session ka unsealData expired seals ko reject kar deta hai) — read request- aur time-dependent hai. Yahi kaam 'use cache: private' ka hai: cookies()/headers() ko directly padhta hai, result sirf browser me rehta hai, server par kabhi nahi. Iske bajay server par cache karna ho to ek value (jaise userId) extract karke plain 'use cache' / 'use cache: remote' me pass karo.

%
tsx
// lib/session.ts
import 'server-only'
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
import { sealData, unsealData } from 'iron-session'
export type SessionData = { userId?: string }
const COOKIE_NAME = 'app_session'
const password = process.env.SESSION_PASSWORD!
export async function getSession(): Promise<SessionData> {
  const cookie = (await cookies()).get(COOKIE_NAME)?.value
  if (!cookie) return {}
  return unsealData<SessionData>(cookie, { password })
}
% %
tsx
// lib/auth.ts
import 'server-only'
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
import { getSession } from './session'
import { findUserById } from './data'
export type User = { id: string; name: string }
export async function getCurrentUser(): Promise<User> {
  'use cache: private'
  const { userId } = await getSession()
  if (!userId) redirect('/login')
  const user = await findUserById(userId)
  if (!user) redirect('/login')
  return { id: user.id, name: user.name }
}
%

redirect() koi value return karne ke bajay rendering ko interrupt karne ke liye throw karta hai, isliye wo cached nahi hota — sirf ek resolved user hi cache hota hai. use cache: private cookies(), headers(), searchParams accept karta hai — lekin connection() nahi.

Step 2 — Page ko block kiye bina user ko dikhao: session padhne wala component <Suspense> ke peeche baitha hona chahiye; Cache Components ke saath, boundary ke bahar cookies() padhna ek build error hai. Boundary ke bahar ki har cheez static shell me prerender hoti hai (agar wo static ya 'use cache' ki hui hai aur runtime data nahi padhti). Sirf boundary ke peeche wala hissa wait karta hai. Session read ko layout ke top level se bhi bahar rakho — layout me top-level await {children} samet poore segment ko rok deta hai; use boundary ke andar ek component me dhakel do. Reads ko ek function (getCurrentUser) me centralized rakhna DAL pattern hai.

%
tsx
export default function Page() {
  return (
    <main>
      <Announcements /> {/* 'use cache' — prerenders into static shell */}
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading your dashboard…</p>}>
        <Dashboard /> {/* reads session, streams in */}
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  )
}
%

Step 3 — User ko components ke beech share karo: ek baar padho, usi boundary ke andar se kai Server + Client Components ko do. Server Components getCurrentUser() ko directly call karte hain. Bina prop drilling ke Client Components ke liye: promise ko ek baar banao, context se pass karo, use() se unwrap karo. Kyunki getCurrentUser request ko padhta hai, iska promise Suspense boundary ke andar banao, layout ke top par nahi. Har consumer use apni boundary ke peeche resolve karta hai, isliye shared chrome session ka wait kiye bina render ho jata hai. Client ko sirf wahi expose karo jiski use zaroorat hai — raw session ke bajay ek narrow { id, name } return karo; sensitive fields ko client se door rakhne ke liye taintUniqueValue use karo.

Step 4 — Session-derived data ko cache karo (do tareeke): (a) userId ko plain 'use cache' me pass karo — result server par, id se keyed (id cache key ka hissa ban jata hai), cacheTag se invalidatable. (b) 'use cache: private' ke andar padho — sirf browser me, server par kabhi nahi (ye tab mayne rakhta hai jab requirements kuch data ko server par ephemerally bhi store karne se rokti hon). Plain use cache cookies() nahi padh sakta, isliye exported getter user ko resolve karke sirf id pass karta hai:

%
tsx
// lib/data.ts
import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
import { getCurrentUser } from './auth'
export async function getNotes() {
  const user = await getCurrentUser()
  return getNotesByUserId(user.id)
}
async function getNotesByUserId(userId: string) {
  'use cache'
  cacheTag(`notes:${userId}`)
  cacheLife('minutes')
  return db.query.notes.findMany({ where: (notes, { eq }) => eq(notes.userId, userId) })
}
%

getNotesByUserId ko unexported rakho taaki koi caller dusri id pass karke kisi aur user ke notes na mang sake — exported getter ke andar user ko resolve karna hi ise safe banata hai. Getter ke andar getCurrentUser() call karna private cache ko hit karta hai, isliye session dobara nahi padha jata. Warning: cache keys aur tags plain text me store hote hain — arguments/captured variables cache key me serialize ho jate hain, cacheTag values jaise likhe hon waise store hoti hain; koi bhi hashed nahi hota. Key/tag kisi stable identifier jaise user id par rakho; secrets aur sensitive PII (tokens, passwords, raw emails) ko arguments aur tags se bahar rakho. Server-side plain use cache in-memory best effort hai (pressure me evict ho jata hai, serverless instances ke paar persist nahi hota) — durable shared storage ke liye 'use cache: remote' use karo.

Step 5 — Session-derived data ko update karo: jab koi Server Action user data badle, to usi tag ke saath updateTag call karo. Action ke andar session ko dobara padho taaki wo client par bharosa karne ke bajay khud ko authorize kare:

%
ts
'use server'
export async function addNote(formData: FormData) {
  const { userId } = await getSession()
  if (!userId) redirect('/login')
  const note = String(formData.get('note') ?? '').trim()
  if (note) {
    await saveNote(userId, note)
    updateTag(`notes:${userId}`)
  }
}
%

Step 6 — Authenticated navigations ko instant banao: zyada tar automatic hai: 'use cache: private' default profile (5-minute stale) use karta hai jab tak set na kiya jaye; session padhne wala route authenticated content ke saath ek per-session App Shell banata hai, jo per session prefetched + cached hota hai — navigations pehle se hi instant hain. Do cheezein ise aisa rakhti hain: (a) agar tum cacheLife tune karo, to stale ≥ 30 seconds rakho — isse neeche scope prefetching se bahar gir jata hai; (b) jo route URL (params/searchParams) par bhi nirbhar karta hai, use uski taraf ishara karne wale links par <Link prefetch={true}> chahiye (per-link prefetching per-link data ko click se pehle resolve karti hai; iske liye Partial Prefetching chahiye — flag enable karo ya segment par prefetch = 'partial' rakho). Prop wahan jodo jahan wait iske layak ho: har link par ek server invocation (/chat/[id] links wali sidebar har item par keemat chukati hai).

Aam pitfalls: plain use cache ke andar cookies()/headers() throw karte hain; cache keys/tags me secrets/PII (plain text); authorization ke liye client par bharosa — har Server Action aur Route Handler me, data ke kareeb, session ko dobara verify karo.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Cache Components ke saath <Suspense> ke bahar cookies() padhna build error hai.
  • Private cache ke results server tak kabhi nahi pahunchte.
  • stale < 30s prefetching ko khatm kar deta hai.
Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
'use cache: private' kyun exist karta hai (request/time-dependent reads server par cache nahi ho sakte); server caching ke liye extract-and-pass pattern; per-session App Shell; plain-text cache keys/tags ka security matlab; unexported-helper wala safety pattern.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication-with-cache-components
Hissa 26 / 471 · App Router · Guides

How to use Next.js as a backend for your frontend

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How to use Next.js as a backend for your frontend. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How to use Next.js as a backend for your frontend — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Headers, Rate limiting, Verify payloads, Protected resources, Server Components, Server Actions. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Key concepts: Next.js frontend (BFF) pattern ke liye backend ka support karta hai - public endpoint HTTP requests ko sambhalne, kisi bhi content ke prakar (keval HTML) ko lautane, data sroton tak pahunchna, side iphekt karna. create-next-app --api mein ek udaharan route.ts shamil hai. Not ek full backend pratisthapan - yeh ek API parat hai jo public roop se pahunch yogy hai, kisi bhi HTTP request ko sambhalti hai, kisi bhi content ke prakar ko wapas kar sakti hai. Route Handlers , proxy, (Pages Router: API roots) ke saath kaaryaanvayana.

pablik endpoint: Route Handlers public HTTP endpoint hain - koi bhi client unhein access kar sakta hai. route.ts/route.js file convention (export function GET(request: Request) {} us path par GET sambhalta hai). try/catch ka upyog karein; never error sandesh mein sanvedanshil jankari ko expose karta hai client ko bheja gaya. authentication/authorization ke saath pratibndhit pahunch (authentication guide dekhein).

Content prakar: JSON, XML, images, files, plain paatha. common endpoints ke liye file convention: sitemap.xml, opengraph-image.jpg/twitter-image, favicon/app icon/apple-icon, manifest.json, robots.txt. custom logon: llms.txt, rss.xml, .well-known — e.g. app/rss.xml/route.ts RSS ko karya karta hai (XML string ka build, new Response(rssFeed, { headers: new Headers({ 'content-type': 'application/xml' }) }) ko wapas karta hai). Sanitize kisi bhi input ka upyog markup generated karne ke liye kiya jata hai.

Content negotiation: rewrites ka upyog karta hai, jo Accept - e.g par aadharit ek hi URL se vibhinn prakar ki content ki serve karne ke liye mel khaati hai. docs site browsers ko HTML pradan karti hai, usi /docs/… URL se AI agents ko kachcha markdown. Rewrite: source: '/docs/:slug*', destination: '/docs/md/:slug*', has: [{ type: 'header', key: 'accept', value: '(.*)text/markdown(.*)' }]. app/docs/md/[...slug]/route.ts par Route Handler ne Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8 aur Vary: Accept ke saath markdown lautaya (tells cache) body svikarya header par nirbhar karta hai - iske bina ek sajha cache ek browser ya iske viprit markdown ki serve kar sakta hai). generateStaticParams pre-renders markdown variants for build time for Edge serving. test: curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://example.com/docs/getting-started. not: /docs/md/... abhi bhi seedhe accessible hai - yadi required ho to proxy ke madhyam se apekshit accept header ke bina block direct request; advanced negotiation ke liye phir likhne ke bajaay proxy ka upyog karein.

Consuming request payload: request.json(), .formData(), .text(). GET/HEAD koi body nahi le jata hai. Validate data ise any pranaliyon se gujarane se pahle. aap keval request nikaay Once ko parh sakte hain - phir se parhne ke liye request (request.clone()) ko klon kar sakte hain; mool pheinkon par ek dusra padha.

Manipulating data: multiple sroton se Route Handlers transform/filter/aggregate, frontend aur internal pranaliyon se bahar tark rakhte hue, server ke liye ophlod hevee kampyooteshan (client battery/data bachata hai). udaharan: POST mausam endpoint parhne { lat, lng } JSON body se, upstream, parsing lane, JSON lautne. not: udaharan URL mein bhoo-sthan lagane se bachne ke liye POST ka upyog karta hai (GET cached/logged ho sakta hai, sanvedanshil jankari ko expose kar sakta hai).

Proxying to a backend: phoravard with rewrites or proxy rewrite; jab aapko validation ki requirement hoti hai, to backend ke saath authenticated karein, ya pratikriya ko badalane ki requirement hoti hai, to ek Route Handler ka upyog karein. backend only headers/credentials ko bhejein, iski zaroorat hai - pratyek aane wale header ki pratilipi banane ke liye user ke Cookie aur Authorization ko bhi agreshit karta hai. yadi aap ek kredeinshiyal sanlagn karte hain, to sunishchit karein ki request kisi any server tak nahi pahunch sakta hai. udaharan pattern: phiksd ENDPOINTS map ('checkout' → '/v1/checkout', 'orders/preview' → '/v1/orders/preview'), catch-ol app/api/[...slug]/route.ts; agyat path → 404; valid request (isValidRequest(request.clone())) → 400 yadi invalid ho; redirect: 'error' ke saath upstream prapt karein, server-side Authorization: Bearer ${process.env.API_TOKEN}, request.text() se body; upstream viphalta → 502. kyonki upstream path map se aata hai, request nahi hai URL, ek kolar kisi any destination par request/token ko point nahi kar sakta hai. Caveat: yeh pure request + memory mein upstream pratikriya ko padhta hai - bare payloads/streaming ke liye iske bajaay phir se likhne ka upyog karta hai.

NextRequest / NextResponse: Route Handlers aur Proxy mein upalabdh web Request/Response ke eksteinshana. donon read/manipulate kukeeza. NextRequest.nextUrl parsed maan (pathname, search params) ko expose karta hai. NextResponse helper: next(), json(), redirect(), rewrite(). NextRequest asaainebal hai jahan Request ki ummid hai; NextResponse jahan Response ki ummid hai.

Webhooks aur callback URL: Route Handlers ko third-party event notifications prapt hoti hain - e.g. CMS webhook: REVALIDATE_SECRET_TOKEN (401 yadi galat hai) ke khilaf token khoj param ko verify karein, tag (400 yadi lapta ho), revalidateTag(tag, 'max') ko call karein, { success: true } ko wapas karein. Callback URLs: pratikriya ko verify karein, redirect karein — prevent open redirects: keval usi mool destination (destination.origin!== request.nextUrl.origin → 400) ki permission dein; redirect pratikriya (response.cookies.set({ value: token, name: '_token', path: '/', secure: true, httpOnly: true, expires: undefined }) — session cookie) par session cookie set karein.

Redirects: Route Handler ke andar next/navigation se redirect('https://nextjs.org/') (). permanentRedirect

Proxy: ek proxy file prati project; config.matcher target patha. request tak pahunchne se pahle ek pratikriya generated karne ke liye proxy ka upyog karein - e.g. isAuthenticated(request) → 401 JSON ke saath get /api/:function*; NextResponse.rewrite ke madhyam se /proxy-this-path → https://nextjs.org ko phir se likhna; /v1/docs → /v2/docs ko request.nextUrl.pathname ko mute karke phir se nirdeshit karein. NextResponse.redirect(request.nextUrl)

Security:

  • Headers: jaanboojh kar samjho — Proxy me NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } }) tumhare apne server ko bheje jane wale headers modify karta hai (client ke contact me nahi); new Response(..., { headers }) / NextResponse.json(..., { headers }) / response.headers.set(...) headers client ko wapas bhejta hai (sensitive values dikh sakte hain).
  • Rate limiting: code me lagu karo (jaise checkRateLimit(request) → 429 { error: 'Rate limit exceeded' }) plus host features. In-memory counters per-instance track karte hain aur restart par reset ho jate hain — multi-instance apps ke liye shared store ya host ki rate limiting use karo.
  • Payloads verify karo: aane wale data par kabhi bharosa mat karo — content type/size validate karo, XSS ke khilaf sanitize karo, user-generated static assets ke liye dedicated services use karo (browser upload → DB me returned URI store karke request size kam karo).
  • Protected resources: credentials hamesha verify karo; sirf Proxy par bharosa mat karo. Route Handler me check sirf tab chalta hai jab handler chalta hai — agar koi response max-age/s-maxage ke saath Cache-Control: public set karti hai, to CDN use bina handler bulaye serve kar sakta hai, isliye credential checks/rate limiting cached requests par lagu nahi hoti — sirf wo responses cache karo jo URL ke saath kisi ke liye bhi safe hon. Responses aur logs se sensitive/unnecessary data strip karo. Credentials/API keys regularly rotate karo.

Preflight request: OPTIONS puchhta hai ki ek request ki permission hai (origin/method/headers). yadi OPTIONS ko define nahi kiya gaya hai, to Next.js ise automatic roop se jodta hai aur any define tarikon (CORS) par aadharit Allow set karta hai.

Library pattern: factory pattern - ek third-party ke library, export const GET = handler / export { handler as POST } se createHandler({...}); library method / pathname dwara anukoolita. library ek proxy factory (export default createMiddleware()) bhi pradan kar sakte hain; dhyaan dein third-party libs abhi bhi proxy "middleware" kah sakte hain.

Caveats:

  • Server Components: data seedhe uske source se fetch karo, Route Handlers ke through NAHI. Build par prerender hue Server Components file system/cache use kar sakte hain (build time par koi server sun nahi raha hota). Route Handlers ke through aane wale on-demand Server Components slow hote hain (extra HTTP round trip). Server-side fetch ko full URL chahiye → HTTP round trip ek external server tak bhi (dev me server; runtime par public domain). Client-side fetching client-only Web APIs (geo-location, Storage, Audio, File) aur frequently polling data ke liye hai — SWR/React Query use karo.
  • Server Actions: client se mutations ke liye; ve queued hote hain — unhe data fetching ke liye use karna sequential execution lata hai.
  • export mode: static site, koi runtime server nahi; sirf GET Route Handlers supported, dynamic = 'force-static' ke saath — static HTML/JSON/TXT files generate karne ke liye use hota hai.
  • Deployment environment: kuch hosts Route Handlers ko per-request ephemeral units ki tarah deploy karte hain — requests ke beech koi shared data nahi, file system writes support nahi ho sakte, lambe handlers timeout ho sakte hain, WebSockets kaam nahi karega (response ke baad connection band ho jata hai).

Dhyaan Do: request body parhne yogy ek bar (phir parhne ke liye band); Cache-Control: public + CDN bypass handler eth check; callback mein khula-redirect jokhim; sabhi header ki pratilipi user kredeinshiyal upstream ko aage badhati hai.

Yaad Rakho — Asli Baat (Interview ke liye)
BFF pattern gunjaish (API parat, full backend nahi); phir likhne + Vary: Accept ke madhyam se content negotiation; kyon Server Components ko Route Handlers ke madhyam se nahi prapt hona chahiye; backend prokseeing ke liye ENDPOINTS-map svikarya pattern; webhook revalidation flow; export mode Route Handler boundary.
