How to build micro-frontends using multi-zones and Next.js

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How to build micro-frontends using multi-zones and Next.js. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How to build micro-frontends using multi-zones and Next.js — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Multi-Zones, Navigation behavior, How to define a zone, How to route requests to the right zone, Routing with proxy, Linking between zones. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Main Points — Pehle Ye Samjho

  • Multi-Zones ek micro-frontend tareeka hai: ek domain par bade application ko chhote-chhote Next.js applications me baant do, har application paths ke ek set ko serve karta hai. Ye tab kaam ka hai jab kuch pages ka sangrah baaki app se khaas related nahi hota. Un pages ko alag zone me le jaane se har application ka size kam hota hai (build time behtar hota hai, aur sirf ek zone ko chahiye wala code hat jata hai) aur applications decouple ho jate hain — domain par dusre applications apni pasand ka framework bhi use kar sakte hain.
  • Example split: /blog/* (blog posts), /dashboard/* (logged-in dashboard pages), /* (website ka baaki hissa). Ek hi domain par teen applications serve hote hain — user ko ek jaise dikhte hain, lekin independently develop aur deploy hote hain.
  • Example: With Zones (github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-zones).
  • Navigation behavior: ek hi zone ke andar navigation soft hota hai (page reload nahi hota — jaise / → /products). Zones ke beech navigation hard hota hai (current page ke resources unload hote hain, naye page ke load hote hain — jaise / → /dashboard). Jo pages aksar ek saath visit hote hain, unhe ek hi zone me rakho taaki hard navigation se bacha ja sake.

kaise ek field ko define karne ke liye

  • Ek zone ek normal Next.js application hota hai, bas dusre zones ke pages/static files se conflict bachane ke liye ek assetPrefix config extra hoti hai:
js
// next.config.js
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  assetPrefix: '/blog-static',
}
  • Next.js assets (JS/CSS) assetPrefix ke saath serve hote hain — har zone ke liye /assetPrefix/_next/... ke neeche. Default application, jo un saare paths ko handle karta hai jo kisi zyada specific zone ko route nahi hue, use assetPrefix ki zaroorat nahi hoti.
  • Next.js 15 se purane versions me static assets handle karne ke liye ek extra rewrite chahiye tha — Next.js 15 me ye ab zaroori nahi hai:
js
// next.config.js (pre-15 only)
const nextConfig = {
  assetPrefix: '/blog-static',
  async rewrites() {
    return {
      beforeFiles: [
        {
          source: '/blog-static/_next/:path+',
          destination: '/_next/:path+',
        },
      ],
    }
  },
}

kaise sahi field ke liye request route karne ke liye

  • Requests ko sahi zone (alag application) tak route karna hota hai. Koi bhi HTTP proxy chalega, lekin Next.js applications me se ek poore domain ke liye rewrites se bhi routing kar sakta hai — har us path ke liye ek rule jo dusra zone serve karta hai, plus static assets ke rules:
js
// next.config.js
async rewrites() {
    return [
        {
            source: '/blog',
            destination: `${process.env.BLOG_DOMAIN}/blog`,
        },
        {
            source: '/blog/:path+',
            destination: `${process.env.BLOG_DOMAIN}/blog/:path+`,
        },
        {
            source: '/blog-static/:path+',
            destination: `${process.env.BLOG_DOMAIN}/blog-static/:path+`,
        }
    ];
}
  • destination ek URL hona chahiye jo zone serve karta ho (scheme + domain) — zone ka production domain, ya local dev me localhost.
  • URL path har zone ke liye unique hona chahiye — /blog serve karne wale do zones routing conflict paida karenge.
  • Proxy ke saath routing: latency kam rakhne ke liye rewrites recommended hain, lekin jab dynamic decision chahiye ho to proxy kaam karta hai — jaise feature flag par based decision, jisme migration ke dauraan ek path kahin aur route hota hai:
js
// proxy.js
export async function proxy(request) {
  const { pathname, search } = request.nextUrl
  if (pathname === '/your-path' && myFeatureFlag.isEnabled()) {
    return NextResponse.rewrite(`${rewriteDomain}${pathname}${search}`)
  }
}

jonon ke beech sanbandh

  • Dusre zone ke path ka link plain <a> tag se banao, Next.js <Link> component se nahi — <Link> kisi bhi relative path ko prefetch aur soft-navigate karne ki koshish karta hai, jo zones ke beech kaam nahi karta.

code sajha karna

  • Zone applications kisi bhi repository me reh sakte hain; code share karne ke liye monorepo aksar convenient hota hai. Alag repos wale zones public/private npm packages ke through code share kar sakte hain. Kyunki zones alag-alag samay par release ho sakte hain, feature flags zones ke aas-paas features ko enable/disable karne ke liye useful hote hain.

bahu-jon ke saath Server Actions

  • User-facing origin ko explicitly allow karna chahiye, kyunki user jis domain ka saamna karta hai wo kai applications serve kar sakta hai. next.config.js me:
js
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    serverActions: {
      allowedOrigins: ['your-production-domain.com'],
    },
  },
}
  • Detail ke liye experimental.serverActions.allowedOrigins dekho.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Cross-zone link ke liye <Link> use karna — prefetch/soft navigation fail ho jayega; <a> use karo.
  • Do zones ka ek hi path claim karna — routing conflict; path har zone ke liye unique rakho.
  • serverActions.allowedOrigins bhool jana — Server Actions zones ke beech toot jate hain.
  • Non-default zones par assetPrefix bhool jana — zones ke beech asset conflicts honge.
  • Aksar ek saath visit hone wale pages ko alag zones me rakhna — har baar hard navigation force hoga.

interview points

  • Multi-Zones kya hain aur kab use karein (ek domain par pages ke groups, independent deployment, alag frameworks).
  • Zones me soft vs hard navigation; assetPrefix ka purpose aur pre-15 rewrite; rewrites vs proxy (latency vs dynamic decision); zones ke paar <a> vs <Link>; code sharing (monorepo/npm) + releases sync karne ke liye feature flags; serverActions.allowedOrigins.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/multi-zones
Hissa 64 / 471 · App Router · Guides

Handling connectivity drops

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Handling connectivity drops. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Handling connectivity drops — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Experimental feature, Enable offline detection and see the default behavior, App-wide banner, Retry Server Actions after the network returns, Testing, Without Cache Components. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Main Points — Pehle Ye Samjho

  • Experimental feature (badge: Experimental) — change ke adheen, production ke liye recommended nahi; GitHub ke through feedback do.
  • Problem: client me ek soft navigation, data fetch ya mutation ke dauraan network failures; UI bina explicit handling ke break ho jati hai ya tumhe ek fallback UI banana padta hai jo user ko retry karne ko kehta hai.
  • experimental.useOffline enable hone ke saath, ek failed navigation, RSC data fetch, prefetch, ya Server Action ab network down hone par throw nahi karta — Next.js use connection wapas aane tak pending rakhta hai.
  • Jabki pending hai, UI apni loading state (Suspense fallback, ya Server Action ke liye ek pending transition) me rehta hai — ek slow server jaisa dikhta hai. Application offline hone par users ko feedback dene ke liye useOffline hook use karo.
  • Ek Client Component ke andar seedhe fetch() se issued requests, ya ek client-side data library (React Query, SWR) ke through, us library ki apni retry policy ke under rehte hain. Framework ke detection/polling behavior ke liye useOffline config reference dekho.
  • Example: live metrics page jo har request par fresh data fetch karta hai + ek ping form jo ek Server Action call karta hai. Source: github.com/nextjs/use-offline; live demo: use-offline.labs.vercel.dev. Demo me /without-feedback (generic loading fallback) aur /with-feedback (connectivity-aware fallback) hai.

offline pata lagane mein enable aur default behavior dekhein

  • experimental.useOffline enable karo. Guide Cache Components + Partial Prefetching bhi enable karta hai: Cache Components tumhe Suspense boundary ko uncached data ke jitna paas ho sake rakhne deta hai, App Shell uske chaaron or render hota hai; Partial Prefetching us App Shell ko wo unit banata hai jo ek <Link> prefetch karta hai, isliye ye offline navigation hone par render karne ke liye ready hai.
ts
// next.config.ts
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
  experimental: {
    useOffline: true,
  },
}

export default nextConfig
  • Tumhe dashboard ke liye ek <Link> wala ek source page bhi chahiye — Next.js viewport me kisi bhi <Link> ke App Shell ko prefetch karta hai, aur wahi prefetch shell ko offline available banata hai.
  • Dashboard: ek static shell + <Suspense> ke andar ek uncached data section; getLiveMetrics ek uncached function hai jo har call par network hit karta hai:
tsx
// app/dashboard/page.tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { getLiveMetrics } from '../lib/data'

export default function Dashboard() {
  return (
    <section>
      <h1>Live metrics</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading...</p>}>
        <MetricsTable />
      </Suspense>
    </section>
  )
}

async function MetricsTable() {
  const { services } = await getLiveMetrics()
  // render services
}
  • Flow: home load karo; dashboard shell prefetch hota hai. Offline jao aur /dashboard par click karo — title/container static shell se render hote hain; Loading... fallback indefinitely rehta hai kyunki getLiveMetrics() complete nahi ho sakta (slow server jaisa hi spinner). Wapas online toggle karo — metrics table automatically stream in hoti hai; Next.js ne apne aap retry kiya, koi client code nahi.
  • Limitation: ye sirf prefetched routes me soft navigations aur current page se Server Action calls par lagu hota hai. Offline hote hue ek full page reload abhi bhi fail hota hai (browser ko HTML deliver karne ke liye network chahiye); full offline load ke liye ek service worker chahiye (PWAs guide dekho).

Suspense Fallback (useOffline hook) ke andar connectivity ki report karein

  • Jab browser ek offline event fire karta hai, ya jab ek navigation, prefetch ya Server Action fetch fail ho jata hai, to useOffline true return karta hai. Jab background connectivity check succeed hota hai to ye false par wapas aata hai. navigator.onLine se zyada reliable, jo sirf OS network interfaces reflect karta hai aur bina upstream internet wale WiFi ke liye bhi true report kar sakta hai.
  • Client components hook se apna message uthate hain:
tsx
// app/dashboard/connectivity-fallback.tsx
'use client'

import { useOffline } from 'next/offline'

export function ConnectivityFallback() {
  const isOffline = useOffline()

  return (
    <p>
      {isOffline
        ? 'Waiting for connection to load this section...'
        : 'Loading...'}
    </p>
  )
}
  • Note: useOffline SSR aur initial hydration ke dauraan false return karta hai; pehla sahi value wo hai jo browser app mount hone ke baad report karta hai.
  • Ise Suspense fallback ke roop me pass karo: <Suspense fallback={<ConnectivityFallback />}>. Offline, fallback "Is segment ko load karne ke liye connection ka wait ho raha hai" padhta hai; connectivity restore hone par metrics stream in hote hain aur fallback gayab ho jata hai.
  • App-wide banner: fallback sirf apne page par dikhta hai jabki uski boundary wait karti hai — root layout me ek banner jodo taaki connectivity state har jagah dikhai de:
tsx
// app/offline-banner.tsx
'use client'

import { useOffline } from 'next/offline'

export function OfflineBanner() {
  const isOffline = useOffline()

  if (!isOffline) {
    return null
  }

  return (
    <div role="status">
      Offline. Pending requests will retry once you are back online.
    </div>
  )
}
  • <OfflineBanner /> ko root layout me jodo. Banner har route par dikhta hai jabki offline ho, connectivity wapas aane par chhup jata hai. Rule of thumb: pending loading state aksar apps ke liye kaafi hai; app me connectivity communicate karne ke liye root-layout banner jodo; content load hone wali jagah ke liye Suspense fallback ko connectivity-aware banao.
  • Wahi pattern parameterized routes tak extend hota hai: /chats/[id] apna shared App Shell render karta hai jab /chats/42 par offline navigate karte ho; <Suspense> ke peeche dynamic messages connection wapas aane par load hote hain. Agar route click se pehle per-link URL data prefetch karta hai, to /chats/42 wait karne ke bajaye us prefetch se turant apne messages bhejta hai, offline bhi (Optimizing prefetching dekho).

network return ke baad Retry Server Actions

  • Flag ke bina, network down hone par call kiya gaya Server Action ek error throw karta hai aur awaited Promise reject ho jata hai — form ko use catch karna chahiye aur decide karna chahiye: error dikhana, retry karna, ya queue karna.
  • experimental.useOffline ke saath, ye failure tumhare code tak kabhi pahunchti hi nahi — call connection wapas aane tak pending rehta hai, request dobara chalta hai, aur awaited Promise server ke response ke saath resolve hota hai. Koi try/catch nahi, koi retry pass nahi, koi reconnect handler nahi.
  • Button phir bhi frozen dikhta hai, lekin — connectivity-aware labels ke liye useOffline ko useTransition ke saath jodo:
tsx
// app/ping/ping-form.tsx
'use client'

import { useState, useTransition } from 'react'
import { useOffline } from 'next/offline'
import { ping } from './actions'

export function PingForm() {
  const [pongs, setPongs] = useState<string[]>([])
  const [pending, startTransition] = useTransition()
  const isOffline = useOffline()

  function handleSubmit() {
    startTransition(async () => {
      const pong = await ping()
      setPongs((prev) => [pong, ...prev])
    })
  }

  const label = pending
    ? isOffline
      ? 'Pinging (offline, will retry)...'
      : 'Pinging...'
    : 'Ping'

  return (
    <form action={handleSubmit}>
      <button type="submit" disabled={pending}>
        {label}
      </button>
      <ul>
        {pongs.map((t) => (
          <li key={t}>{t}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </form>
  )
}
  • Offline hote hue Ping click karna button disable karta hai aur use "Ping (offline, retrying)" label karta hai. Connectivity restore hona pending ping() call ko resolve karta hai, timestamp apply karta hai, aur label wapas badal deta hai — koi dusra click nahi, koi client-side retry code nahi.
  • Note: offline hote hue, ek pending Server Action ke dauraan ek link par click karne se kuch nahi dikh sakta — link ke navigation ko bhi network chahiye aur ye action ki tarah hi usi connectivity signal ke peeche queue hota hai; dono connection wapas aane par resolve hote hain.

Testing

  • next build && next start ke saath test karo — dev mode offline behavior ke liye reliable reference NAHI hai. Chrome: DevTools → Network → Offline; Firefox: Network Monitor throttling menu. Real-world: airplane mode, WiFi disconnect karo, ya network cable unplug karo.

cache component ke bina

  • Ek route-level loading.tsx wahi kaam karta hai — ye Next.js ko route ke shell ke roop me prefetch karne ke liye ek boundary deta hai, isliye shell offline render hota hai aur page network wapas aane par resume hota hai (dekho ki loading.tsx prefetching kaise kaam karta hai). useOffline hook, banner aur Server Action retry sab wahi behave karte hain.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Offline kaam karne ke liye ek full page reload ki ummeed karna — sirf prefetched routes me soft navigations aur Server Actions cover hote hain; full offline load ke liye ek service worker (PWA) chahiye.
  • useOffline ke bajaye navigator.onLine use karna — ye WiFi-with-no-upstream-internet ko miss karta hai.
  • Dev mode me offline behavior test karna — unreliable; production build use karo.
  • Direct client fetch() / React Query / SWR requests ko framework dwara retry karne ki ummeed karna — ve apni retry policy rakhte hain.
  • useOffline SSR/hydration ke dauraan false return karta hai — pehle value ko sahi mat samjho.

interview points

  • Kya experimental.useOffline badalta hai (failed nav/fetch/action throw karne ke bajaye pending rehta hai + auto-retries) aur iska scope (sirf prefetched routes me soft navs + Server Actions).
  • useOffline vs navigator.onLine; connectivity-aware fallback + root-layout banner pattern; useTransition ke through offline-aware Server Action button labels.
  • Kyun prefetched App Shell offline navigation possible banata hai; Cache Components ke barabar loading.tsx.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/offline-support
Hissa 65 / 471 · App Router · Guides

How to set up instrumentation with OpenTelemetry

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai How to set up instrumentation with OpenTelemetry. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: How to set up instrumentation with OpenTelemetry — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: OpenTelemetry, Getting started with @vercel/otel, Manual OpenTelemetry configuration, Testing your instrumentation, Deployment, Using the OpenTelemetry Collector. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Main Points — Pehle Ye Samjho

  • Observability (logging, metrics, tracing) app behavior/performance samajhne aur optimize karne ke liye crucial hai; jaise apps zyada complex bante hain, issues diagnose karna mushkil hota jata hai. Observability developers ko badi problems banne se pehle issues proactively address karne deti hai aur UX improve karti hai. Next.js apps ke liye recommended.
  • OpenTelemetry recommended instrumentation approach hai — platform-agnostic hai, isliye tum code badle bina observability providers badal sakte ho. Use hue terms: Span, Trace, Exporter (OpenTelemetry Observability Primer dekho). Next.js out of the box OpenTelemetry instrumentation support karta hai — Next.js khud pehle se instrumented hai.

shuru ho raha hai @vercel/otel

  • OpenTelemetry setup verbose hai; @vercel/otel package tumhe jaldi start karata hai. Install karo:
bash
pnpm add @vercel/otel @opentelemetry/sdk-logs @opentelemetry/api-logs @opentelemetry/instrumentation
  • Project root me instrumentation.ts (ya .js) banao (ya src/ ke andar agar use kar rahe ho).
ts
// instrumentation.ts
import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'

export function register() {
  registerOTel({ serviceName: 'next-app' })
}
  • Extra config options ke liye @vercel/otel docs dekho. Placement rules (Instrumentation guide jaisi hi): root, app//pages/ ke andar nahi; agar pageExtensions ek suffix jodta hai, to instrumentation filename ko match karne ke liye update karo. Example: with-opentelemetry (github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-opentelemetry).

manual OpenTelemetry config

  • Agar @vercel/otel tumhari needs ke hisaab se nahi hai, to manually configure karo. Install karo:
bash
pnpm add @opentelemetry/sdk-node @opentelemetry/resources @opentelemetry/semantic-conventions @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http
  • instrumentation.ts me NodeSDK initialize karo. @vercel/otel ke vipreet, NodeSDK Edge runtime ke saath compatible NAHI hai — use sirf tab import karo jab process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs' ho, jaise ek conditionally imported instrumentation.node.ts ke through:
ts
// instrumentation.ts
export async function register() {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') {
    await import('./instrumentation.node.ts')
  }
}

// instrumentation.node.ts
import { OTLPTraceExporter } from '@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http'
import { resourceFromAttributes } from '@opentelemetry/resources'
import { NodeSDK } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-node'
import { SimpleSpanProcessor } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node'
import { ATTR_SERVICE_NAME } from '@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions'

const sdk = new NodeSDK({
  resource: resourceFromAttributes({
    [ATTR_SERVICE_NAME]: 'next-app',
  }),
  spanProcessor: new SimpleSpanProcessor(new OTLPTraceExporter()),
})
sdk.start()
  • @vercel/otel ke barabar lekin uske exposed options se aage extendable hai. Agar Edge runtime support chahiye, to @vercel/otel use karo.

apne instrumentation ka testing

  • Tumhe locally test karne ke liye ek compatible backend ke saath ek OpenTelemetry collector chahiye — recommended: OpenTelemetry dev environment (github.com/vercel/opentelemetry-collector-dev-setup).
  • Agar ye kaam karta hai, to tum root server span ko GET /requested/pathname labeled dekhoge, us trace ke saare dusre spans uske under nested honge.
  • Next.js default roop se emit hone wale spans se zyada spans trace karta hai — zyada dekhne ke liye, NEXT_OTEL_VERBOSE=1 set karo.

Deployment

  • OpenTelemetry collector use karna: @vercel/otel Vercel aur self-hosting dono par kaam karta hai.
  • Vercel par: OpenTelemetry out of the box kaam karta hai — project ko ek observability provider se connect karne ke liye Vercel ke tracing docs follow karo.
  • Self-hosting: apna khud ka OpenTelemetry collector spin up karo (Collector Getting Started guide follow karo), phir apne platform par Next.js app deploy karo.
  • Custom spans: ek collector required nahi hai — @vercel/otel ya manual config ke saath ek custom exporter use karo.

custom spain

  • OpenTelemetry APIs (@opentelemetry/api) ke saath ek custom span jodo:
ts
import { trace } from '@opentelemetry/api'

export async function fetchGithubStars() {
  return await trace
    .getTracer('nextjs-example')
    .startActiveSpan('fetchGithubStars', async (span) => {
      try {
        return await getValue()
      } finally {
        span.end()
      }
    })
}
  • register function tumhare code ko ek naye environment me chalne se pehle execute hota hai; request handle karne ke dauraan bane spans us request ke trace me jode jate hain.
  • Important: jab instrumentation file load ho rahi ho, ya register ke andar, bane spans automatically ek request trace me shamil nahi hote. Tracer provider install hone se pehle start hue spans (jaise file top level par registerOTel run hone se pehle) record nahi hote; SDK start hone ke baad register ke andar start hue spans ek alag root trace banate hain. Ek request ke hisse ke roop me kaam trace karne ke liye, request handle karne ke dauraan chalne wale code me spans banao (ek page, ek Route Handler, ek API route).

Next.js mein default avdhi

  • Next.js automatically kai spans likhta hai. Attributes OpenTelemetry semantic conventions follow karte hain, plus next namespace ke under custom attributes:
  • next.span_name — span naam ko duplicate karta hai.
  • next.span_type — per span type unique identifier.
  • next.route — route pattern (jaise /[param]/user).
  • next.rsc (true/false) — kya request ek RSC request hai.
  • next.page — internal App Router value (ek specific file ka route jaise page.ts, layout.ts, loading.ts); sirf tab unique hai jab next.route ke saath paired ho (jaise /layout /(groupA)/layout.ts aur /(groupB)/layout.ts dono ko identify kar sakta hai).
  • Default spans:
  • [http.method] [next.route] (BaseServer.handleRequest) — har incoming request ke liye root span; HTTP method, route, target, status code track karta hai. Attributes: http.method, http.status_code, http.route, http.target, next.span_name, next.span_type, next.route.
  • render route (app) [next.route] (AppRender.getBodyResult) — App Router me ek route render karna.
  • fetch [http.method] [http.url] (AppRender.fetch) — tumhare code me executed ek fetch request. Attributes: http.method, http.url, net.peer.name, net.peer.port (agar specified ho). NEXT_OTEL_FETCH_DISABLED=1 ke saath disable ho sakta hai (ek custom instrumentation library ke saath useful).
  • executing api route (app) [next.route] (AppRouteRouteHandlers.runHandler) — App Router me API Route Handler execute karna.
  • getServerSideProps [next.route] (Render.getServerSideProps) — Pages Router SSR data fetching.
  • getStaticProps [next.route] (Render.getStaticProps) — Pages Router SSG data fetching.
  • render route (pages) [next.route] (Render.renderDocument) — document render karna (Pages Router).
  • generateMetadata [next.page] (ResolveMetadata.generateMetadata) — ek page ke liye metadata generate karna (ek hi route me in spans me se kai ho sakte hain).
  • resolve page components (NextNodeServer.findPageComponents) — page components resolve karna.
  • resolve segment modules (NextNodeServer.getLayoutOrPageModule) — ek layout ya page ke liye code module load karna.
  • start response (NextNodeServer.startResponse) — zero-length span marking jab response ka pehla byte bheja gaya tha.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs' par gate kiye bina seedhe instrumentation.ts me NodeSDK use karna — ye Edge-compatible nahi hai; Edge ke liye @vercel/otel use karo.
  • File top level par ya register ke andar spans banana aur unke ek request trace me hone ki ummeed karna — ve alag root traces ban jate hain ya record hi nahi hote.
  • Jab Next.js spans appear nahi hote to NEXT_OTEL_VERBOSE=1 bhool jana.
  • Koi collector/backend locally nahi chal raha — traces kahin nahi jate; dev-environment setup use karo.

interview points

  • Kyun OpenTelemetry (vendor-neutral observability) aur @vercel/otel vs manual NodeSDK setup, Edge-runtime constraint samet.
  • instrumentation.ts/register contract aur NEXT_RUNTIME conditional import.
  • Custom startActiveSpan aur request trace scoping rules ke saath spans.
  • Default span catalog (root BaseServer.handleRequest, AppRender.getBodyResult, AppRender.fetch + NEXT_OTEL_FETCH_DISABLED, route handler, metadata, start response) aur next.* span attributes.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/open-telemetry

Optimizing Prefetching

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Optimizing Prefetching. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Optimizing Prefetching — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Resolve URL data at prefetch time, Cost, Include session data in the shell, Extract and pass, `"use cache: private"`, Defer work to a later stage (prefetch() / navigation()). Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Main Points — Pehle Ye Samjho

  • prefetching user navigate karne se pahle root ke JS, CSS aur RSC payload ko download karta hai, isliye router agle route ko round trip ke bina render karta hai. The Prefetching guide App Router ke default ko cover karta hai.
  • With Cache Components + Partial Prefetching, Next.js ne navigation steps mein server-render output ko load kiya : 1. ek default <Link> route ke App Shell -static output plus ko load karta hai, jo cookies()/headers(), session-vishisht UI parhne ke routes ke liye. usi route ke liye link ise sajha karte hain. 2. <Link prefetch={true}> link ke URL data (searchParams, params) ke aadhar par static/cached content ko bhi load karta hai, jismein sajha shell shamil nahi ho sakta hai. 3. jab user link ka anusaran karta hai, to navigation baki ko render karta hai.
  • prefetch() aur navigation() ka upyog ek baad ke step mein mahnge kaam ko moved karne ke liye karein; static rahne ke liye ek manch ki requirement ke liye ensureStatic ka upyog karein (dekhein rakhne wale page static).
  • recommended: next-partial-prefetching-optimizer kaushal (npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) - UI ko define karta hai jo instant() testing mein chaynit link ke liye taiyar hona chahiye, vartaman behavior ko saabit karta hai, testing ko hare rang mein kaam karta hai.
  • Prerequisites: cacheComponents: true + partialPrefetching: true. yadi route abhi tak tatkal navigation ke liye structured nahi hai, to tatkal navigation guide ke saath shuru karein.

Prefetch samay par URL data ko hal karein

  • navigation se pahle us link ke liye URL data ko hal karne ke liye <Link prefetch={true}> set karein. destination Partial Prefetching (global partialPrefetching ya prati segment prefetch = 'partial') ka upyog karna chahiye.
tsx
// app/page.tsx
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <nav>
      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
        React
      </Link>
      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
        Next.js
      </Link>
    </nav>
  )
}
  • 'auto' ≡ omitting prefetch / undefined - ek sashart mein, default App Shell prefetch (prefetch={isFeatured? true: 'auto'}) ko rakhne wale link ke liye 'auto' wapas laute. keval ek link ke liye prefetching ko disabled karne ke liye prefetch={false} ka upyog karein.
  • udaharan: /search query ke aadhar par ek static shirshak + <Results> list pradan karta hai; search() query dwara parinam cache karta hai:
tsx
// app/search/page.tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'

export default function SearchPage({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/search'>) {
  return (
    <>
      <h1>Search</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<ResultsSkeleton />}>
        <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
      </Suspense>
    </>
  )
}

async function Results({ searchParams }: { searchParams: PageProps<'/search'>['searchParams'] }) {
  const { q } = await searchParams
  return <ResultList items={await search(q)} />
}

async function search(q: string) {
  'use cache'
  return db.search(q)
}
  • prefetch={true} ke bina: App Shell ne <h1> + <Results> ka patan wapas render kiya; query click aur dharaon ke parinam ke baad hal ho jati hai. prefetch={true} ke saath: router click se pahle <Results> ko prati-link prefetch ko hal karne ka request karta hai - q link ke URL se aata hai (purv mein) aur cached search(q) parinam pradan karta hai; click par, parinam turant bina kisi rukavat ke render karte hain.
  • Next.js mein prefetch mein static/cached content shamil hai jab tak ki yeh ek bina padha nahi jata hai, tab ismein aaspas ke <Suspense> boundary se wapsi shamil hai (antim navigation ke liye route ko taiyar karne se pahle).
  • Cost: ne prati-link prefetch ki lagat ko preephechebal link ke anusar server run ki lagat ko generated kiya - isliye prati link mein opt-in karein. un pages par jahan sabhi content static roop se render karne yogy hai, Next.js iske bajaay static cache se prefetch ka karya karta hai. gair-static data tak pahunchne wala ek page prati prefetch generated hota hai jab tak ki navigation tak pahunch ko sthagit nahi kiya jata hai.
  • sheet cache (pahle visit / samapti ke baad): server abhi bhi cached parinam ki computation karta hai - user us pahle navigation par ek spinar dekh sakte hain; baad mein navigation tatkal hote hain jabki cache garm hota hai.
  • searchParams ki tarah, params ko <Suspense> boundary ki requirement hoti hai, jab maan generateStaticParams dwara purvnirdharit hote hain - static roop se known param abhi bhi ek URL ke antargat aata hai. prefetch={true} ke saath ek prati link prefetch manon ko hal karta hai generateStaticParams cover nahi karta hai.

shell mein session data shamil karein

  • prefetch={true} URL data ko hal karta hai; session data ko alag se sambhala jata hai. ek root reading cookies()/headers() ("use cache: private" ke madhyam se sahit) ko apne session data sahit App Shell prapt hota hai, client par prati session cache kiya jata hai aur prati link prefetch ke bina navigation par taiyar hota hai.
  • session data par aadharit ek lookup ko cache lifetime ki requirement hoti hai, jaise search(q) ne URL ke liye kiya tha. do pattern (ke baad "use cache" cached function ke andar cookies() ko call nahi kar sakta):
  • Extract and pass — jab lookup parinam kai satron mein sajha kiya jata hai. cached function ke bahar cookie parhein aur ek tark ke roop mein value ko paas karein; cookies() call cache gunjaish ke bahar rahta hai, tark boundary ko par karta hai, cached function mein ek nishchit hastakshar hota hai, aur entry us par ki jati hai - session value sajha karne wale session entry sajha karte hain:
tsx
// app/dashboard/user-nav.tsx
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

async function UserNav() {
  const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
  const topics = await getTopics(team)
  return (
    <nav>
      {topics.map((topic) => (
        <a key={topic.id} href={topic.href}>
          {topic.label}
        </a>
      ))}
    </nav>
  )
}

async function getTopics(team: string | undefined) {
  'use cache'
  return db.topics.forTeam(team)
}

ek seedhi visit par <UserNav> apne patan ko tab tak dikhata hai jab tak ki lookup hal nahi hota; navigation par App Shell pahle se hi ise hal kar chuka hai (team cookie session data hai jo shell parh sakta hai). usi team par session entry ko sajha karte hain, isliye team ki count ke saath built-in data paimane par yatayat, session count nahi. ek caching directive ke bina kuchh bhi abhi bhi navigation ke baad stream karta hai - ek shell keval vahi rakhta hai jo navigation se pahle taiyar kiya jaa sakta hai.

  • "use cache: private" - jab lookup ek session se juraa hua hai. ek aise karya ke liye cache lifetime ko assign karta hai jo seedhe cookies/headers/runtime data ko padhta hai; parinam keval browser mein cache kiye jate hain, jo us session ke dayre mein aate hain:
tsx
async function getUser() {
  'use cache: private'
  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
  return db.users.findBySession(session)
}

jab runtime data ko call site (e.g) par nahi nikala jaa sakta hai to usi pattern ka upyog karein. gunjaish ke andar sab kuchh usi lifetime ko sajha karta hai - sanbhav ke roop mein runtime data access ke karib "use cache: private" ko Colocate karein. Date.now()

baad ke step (prefetch() / navigation()) ke liye sthagit kaam

  • The App Shell ko ek route mein link dwara sajha kiya jata hai; ek drishyaman <Link prefetch={true}> ke liye prati-link prefetch run; navigation click par chalta hai. user ko kabhi-kabhi link karne ke liye mahnge kaam ke layak nahi ho sakta hai. Uncached kaam pahle se hi prefetches se bahar chhor diya hai; kaishebal kaam ke liye, next/cache un karyon ka export karta hai jo pratyek call ke neeche code ko defer karte hain:
  • prefetch() - prati-link prefetch ya navigation tak code ko define karta hai.
  • navigation() - navigation tak code ko define karta hai.
  • donon hi runtime rendering ke dauraan hi lagu hote hain (ve puri tarah se static route nahi badalate hain). pratyek call us component ko define karta hai jo ise aur uske vanshaj ka wait karta hai; pahle step nikatatam <Suspense> girbaik pradan karte hain, jab iske step run banate hain to diphard subtree dwara replace kiya jata hai. connection() ke viprit, na to subtree request-nirbhar banata hai, isliye iske bhitar karya abhi bhi 'use cache' ka upyog kar sakte hain.
  • Keep mahnge session data App Shell: se bahar ek session key rainking mahnga hai aur dashboard mein har default <Link> ise shell ke liye generated karega. Await prefetch() rainking ke upar to keval ek <Link prefetch={true}> click se pahle ise hal karta hai:
tsx
// app/dashboard/recommendations.tsx
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
import { prefetch } from 'next/cache'

async function Recommendations() {
  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
  await prefetch()
  const items = await rank(session)
  return <List items={items} />
}

async function rank(session?: string) {
  'use cache: private'
  return db.recommendations.rank({ session })
}

session prefetch() se upar padha jata hai, isliye yeh abhi bhi shell mein hal ho jata hai; shell rainking generated nahi karta hai. ek default <Link> mein <Suspense> fallback (advertisement ke dauraan badla gaya); ek <Link prefetch={true}> click se pahle rainking ko hal karta hai. rank apne cache lifetime ko donon mamlon mein rakhta hai. na to function ko cached gunjaish ke andar wait kiya jaa sakta hai - directive neeche diye gaye function par jata hai, kyonki rank yahan karta hai.

  • navigation ke liye Wait: ek inboks jahan pratyek view yarn <Link prefetch={true}> ka upyog karta hai - prefetch mein thred vishay shamil hona chahiye, lekin user ko yeh bekaar kaam karne se pahle har sandesh body ko prapt karna chahiye. apne khud ke <Suspense> boundary mein latest sandesh render karein aur ise load karne se pahle navigation() ka wait karein:
tsx
// app/inbox/[threadId]/thread.tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { navigation } from 'next/cache'

async function LatestMessage({ threadId }: { threadId: string }) {
  await navigation()
  const message = await getLatestMessage(threadId)
  return <p>{message.body}</p>
}

donon queries cache rahte hain (getThreadSummary, getLatestMessage 'use cache' ke saath). prati-link prefetch mein cached vishay + sandesh fallback shamil hai; cached body load jab user dhage ko kholta hai, to baad mein visits ke liye upalabdh rahta hai. bina pakre gaye subtree ko chhorne se bhi ise prefetch se bahar rakha jayega lekin navigation par apna cache lifetime bhi kho dega. 'use cache' content ke liye, ek stale ka samay ≥5 minat client-side router ko pahle navigation ke baad pun: upyog karne data hai; iske neeche, pratyek navigation ise phir se prapt karta hai.

  • Keep the prefetch Static:, jab pratyek cookies(), headers(), params, aur searchParams ka pathan navigation() se neeche baithta hai, to ek runtime prefetch usi output ka build karega - Next.js static output se prefetch ki serve kar sakta hai, aur ek CDN ise cache kar sakta hai, isliye route mein ek link ko server computation ki requirement nahi hai. udaharan: ek static header ke saath ek feed - Stories ne navigation() ko topic cookie parhne se pahle wait kiya:
tsx
// app/feed/page.tsx
async function Stories() {
  await navigation()
  const topic = (await cookies()).get('topic')?.value ?? 'all'
  return <StoryList items={await getStories(topic)} />
}

navigation() ke neeche cookie parhne se prati request prati-link prefetch render nahi kiya jata hai (jo kisi bhi tarah se prefetch ke dauraan hal nahi kiya gaya tha). prefetch() aur App Shell ke liye bhi: jab pratyek cookies()/headers() parh prefetch() ke neeche baithta hai, to shell static production se served jata hai. padhna params/searchParams ko ek runtime shell ki requirement nahi hai - URL data ko sajha shell se bahar rakha gaya hai, lekin yeh runtime par ek prati-link prefetch render bana sakta hai jab tak ki yeh navigation() ke neeche baithta hai.

  • pratyek call ek subtree defer karta hai. pure route ke liye static output ki requirement ke liye (isliye baad mein parivartan request samay rendering ko phir se shuru nahi kar sakta), ensureStatic set (dekhein rakhne wale pages ko static).

test prefetched aur diphard kanteint

  • The Instant navigation guide installing/configuring @next/playwright batata hai. ek client navigation ke liye, destination ke prefetched UI ka inspect karne ke liye instant() ka upyog karein. Partial Prefetching ko apnane ke baad, feature ko enable karne aur uske baad usi daave ko phir se chalane se pahle testing chalaein - yeh UI ko legacy full prefetch se chuna gaya hai jabki iska karyanvayan App Shell ya prati-link prefetch mein chal raha hai.
ts
// e2e/product-navigation.test.ts
import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
import { instant } from '@next/playwright'

test('prefetches the product summary but not reviews', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products')

  await instant(page, async () => {
    await page.click('a[href="/products/baseball-cap"]')
    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')

    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
    ).toBeVisible()
    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
    await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toHaveCount(0)
  })

  await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toBeVisible()
})
  • callback ke andar, link par click karein, destination URL ke liye await karein, yeh dava karein ki kaun see content upalabdh hai; callback navigation jari karne ke baad, antath sthagit content par jor dein. jabki instant() chalata hai, dynamic content ka thahrav hai - yahan product summary UI prefetch kiya gaya hai, samiksha navigation ke liye wait karti hai; antim dava samiksha ki pushti karta hai ki thahrav release ke baad render ki jati hai.
  • dev mein, ek prefetch() ya navigation() ko <Suspense> ke bahar call karne ke liye ek Instant Insight ki satah hoti hai - ek puri tarah se previous route aprabhavit hai, lekin insight yeh pehchanti hai ki yadi route ke baad runtime rendering ki requirement hoti hai to call bina kisi fallback ke content ko sthagit kar dega. generateMetadata() aur generateViewport() mein alag-alag insight hai.

tred-oph

  • jab prefetch={true} ka upyog karein: per ka hissa URL data (full URL, searchParams, ya params ko generateStaticParams dwara hal nahi kiya gaya) par nirbhar karta hai; us hisse mein ek known cache lifetime ( "use cache" / "use cache: private" ke saath eksapresebal); yatayat prati-link server run ko sahi thahraataa hai. cached data ko prefetching karne se iski tazgi nahi badalti hai - agar ek mutation data ko update kar sakta hai, to tag aur cached parinam ko invalid kar sakta hai.
  • jab prefetch App Shell ki tulna mein behatar UI ka production nahi kar sakta to ise chhor dein - pratyek drishyaman <Link prefetch={true}> ek server ko jagaa sakta hai, aur us lagat ko keval tabhi bhugtan kiya jata hai jab click se pahle page ka adhik taiyar ho.
  • root mein little/no URL-data dependency hai - App Shell pahle se hi navigation tatkal banata hai.
  • pratyek request par nirbhar content fresh honi chahiye - prerender usi <Suspense> girbaik par bhi ruk jata hai.
  • root ko shayad hi kabhi navigate kiya jata hai - aap click-through ki parvah kiye bina view link par bhugtan karte hain.
  • ek prati link prefetch sabse achha prayas hai - yeh keval navigation mein madad karta hai jahan yeh click se pahle pura ho jata hai. ek dhimi kanekshan par, kai linkon ka ek feed, ya direct visit, yeh taiyar nahi ho sakta hai aur navigation App Shell par wapas gir jata hai.
  • jab kisi route ke kai link ek bar mein dikhai dete hain (e.g. card ka ek grid), pratyek <Link prefetch={true}> us link ki content ko rokta hai kyonki yeh viewport mein access karta hai - prati card ek server anurodha. iske bajaay irade par prefetch: ek hover-triggered prefetch keval link prapt karta hai jo user ko click karne ki sambhavna hai. default <Link> (no prefetch={true}) keval App Shell load karta hai, isliye yeh aisi koi lagat nahi rakhta hai.

  • Deferring kaam un logon ke liye content paida karne se bachta hai jinka upyog kabhi nahi kiya jaa sakta hai; vyapar band ek navigation hai jo nikatatam <Suspense> girbaik dikha sakta hai jabki nishchit content render karta hai.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • koi URL-data dependency ke saath ek route par prefetch={true} ka upyog karna - kuchh bhi nahi ke liye view link ke anusar server run ka bhugtan karta hai.
  • direct visits ya dhimi kanekshan par taiyar hone ke liye prati-link prefetch ka samna karna - yeh sabse achha prayas hai; navigation App Shell par wapas gir jata hai.
  • ek cached gunjaish ke andar prefetch()/navigation() ko bulana - permission nahi hai; call ke neeche bulaye gaye function par directive dein.
  • Dev mein <Suspense> ke bahar prefetch()/navigation() ko bulana - ek Instant Insight ko sathon par rakhta hai (nishchit karte samay dikhane ke liye koi fallback nahi).
  • estimate session data ki zaroorat hai prefetch={true} - session data bhumi iske bina App Shell mein; prefetch={true} URL data ke liye hai.

interview points

  • teen navigation steps aur kya pratyek contains/costs; prefetch={true} banam default <Link> banam prefetch={false} / 'auto'.
  • eksatraikt-eind-paas banam "use cache: private" session data ke liye shell mein.
  • prefetch() banam navigation() deferral semantics (aur connection() banam); prefetch static rakhne; stale ≥ 5 minat router pun: upyog ke liye niyama.
  • prati link lagat vyapar band (ek server view link ke anusar run; grid ke liye hover-triggered prefetch) aur previous banam deferred content ke liye instant() testing paitarna.

Hissa 67 / 471 · App Router · Guides

Optimizing the Static Shell

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Optimizing the Static Shell. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Optimizing the Static Shell — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Patterns table, Pattern 1: Keep static UI in the shell, Pattern 2: Stream request-time work — push data access down, Move data access into a Server Component, Resolve a promise inline, Pass a promise to a Client Component. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Main Points — Pehle Ye Samjho

  • Cache Components request-time content stream hone ke dauraan ek static shell prerender kar sakta hai. Shell route ke layout, navigation, headings aur focused loading states ko visible rakhta hai, page ko ek broad fallback se replace karne ke bajaye.
  • Cache Components se pehle likhe gaye apps aksar ek layout/page ke top ke paas request data await karte hain — Cache Components ke saath un routes me pehle se hi ek chhota static shell ho sakta hai, kabhi-kabhi sirf ek broad loading state.
  • Ye guide har data read ko use chahiye wale UI tak trace karke shell expand karta hai, reusable kaam cache karke, aur request-time kaam ko focused <Suspense> boundaries ke peeche rakhke — important content ko pehle available rakhte hue aur baaki ke stream in hone par space reserve karte hue.
  • Kai underlying patterns (data access ko UI ke paas le jana, focused <Suspense> ke saath streaming, waterfalls se bachna, stable loading states) dusre App Router apps me bhi useful hain; cache directives aur validation workflow ke liye Cache Components chahiye.
  • Recommended: next-cache-components-optimizer skill (npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-optimizer) — intended shell capture karne ke liye instant() verification loop use karta hai, current behavior prove karta hai, aur passing test ko regression coverage ke roop me rakhta hai. Ye ek client navigation ko bhi target kar sakta hai jiska destination UI turant commit nahi hota; agar destination me pehle se instant UI hai aur tum click se pehle extra URL-specific content chahte ho, to iske bajaye Optimizing prefetching use karo.
  • Prerequisites: cacheComponents enable karo aur route ke blocking validation errors pehle resolve karo (Migrating to Cache Components dekho). Client navigations ke liye, Partial Prefetching par bhi vichaar karo — <Link prefetch={true}> me click se pehle cached URL-specific content shamil ho sakti hai.

pattern talika

Patternise kab prayog kareinResult
shell mein static UI rakheinUI ko data ki requirement nahi haiUI static shell mein render kar sakte hain
stream request-samay par kaamek field ko keval request samay par known data ki requirement hoti haiiski nikatatam <Suspense> fallback pahli bar render kar sakti hai
cache pun: prayojy kaamrequest par parinam ka pun: upyog kiya jaa sakta haipura parinam static shell mein render kar sakte hain

pattern 1: shell mein static UI rakhein

  • Ek <Suspense> boundary control karti hai ki jab ek child suspend hota hai to uska fallback UI ke kis hisse ko replace kare. Static UI ek boundary ke andar bina problem ke baith sakta hai — lekin agar usi boundary me slow/request-time kaam bhi ho, to wo fallback static UI ko bhi temporarily replace kar deta hai.
tsx
// Before: one loading state replaces the whole page
<Suspense fallback={<ProductsSkeleton />}>
  <h1>Products</h1>
  <p>Browse the latest products.</p>
  <LiveInventory />
</Suspense>

// After: only inventory uses the loading state
<main>
  <h1>Products</h1>
  <p>Browse the latest products.</p>
  <Suspense fallback={<InventorySkeleton />}>
    <LiveInventory />
  </Suspense>
</main>
  • Headings, navigation, cached content aur dusri stable UI ko kisi bhi loading state se bahar le jao jisme unhe hona nahi chahiye; boundary ko us chhote region tak le jao jo suspend ho sakta hai. Jab primary heading ya koi dusra LCP candidate reusable data par depend karta hai, to us data ko cache karo taaki completed content shell me render ho; agar data ko request ka wait karna chahiye, to uski loading state ko focused rakho.

pattern 2: stream request-samay par kaam - data access ko push karein

  • Kuch data tab tak known nahi ho sakta jab tak koi request na aaye, use per-request recompute karna chahiye, ya uski cache lifetime prerendering ke liye bahut chhoti hai. Agar ek layout/page use top ke paas await kar raha hai, to ye poore page ko block kar sakta hai. Result chahiye wale region ko split karo aur sirf us region ko suspend hone do.
  • Ek Server Component me data access move karo: page ke top par params + ek DB query await karne (heading ko block karna) ke bajaye, params ko ek <Suspense>-wrapped Product component ko Promise ke roop me pass karo jo use await aur fetch karta hai:
tsx
// After: only the product region waits
import { Suspense } from 'react'

export default function ProductPage({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Product</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<ProductSkeleton />}>
        <Product params={params} />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  )
}

async function Product({ params }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug)
  return <ProductDetails product={product} />
}
  • cookies()/headers() — jaise ek dashboard layout turant DashboardShell render karta hai ek UserMenu (cookie-reading) ke saath <Suspense fallback={<UserMenuSkeleton />}> ke peeche.
  • Ek Promise inline resolve karo: ek chhote region ke liye, kisi dusre component ki zaroorat nahi — boundary ke andar .then() ke saath params/searchParams/ek dusra Promise inline resolve karo:
tsx
<Suspense fallback={<ProductTabsSkeleton />}>
  {searchParams.then(({ tab = 'details' }) => (
    <ProductTabs activeTab={tab} />
  ))}
</Suspense>
  • Ek Client Component ko Promise pass karo: parent chart data await nahi karta (parent ka static UI wapas render hota hai) — bina await kiye request start karo, <Suspense> ke peeche Client Component ko Promise pass karo; Client Component use React ke use() ke saath unwrap karta hai:
tsx
// app/dashboard/page.tsx — After
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { getActivity } from '@/app/lib/data'
import { ActivityChart } from './activity-chart'

export default function DashboardPage() {
  const activityPromise = getActivity()

  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<ActivityChartSkeleton />}>
      <ActivityChart dataPromise={activityPromise} />
    </Suspense>
  )
}

// activity-chart.tsx ('use client')
import { use } from 'react'

export function ActivityChart({ dataPromise }: { dataPromise: Promise<Activity[]> }) {
  const activity = use(dataPromise)
  return <Chart data={activity} />
}
  • URL data ke liye, ek Client Component aksar Promise receive karne ke bajaye useParams() / useSearchParams() call kar sakta hai — dono ek client navigation ke dauraan synchronously resolve hote hain kyunki router ke paas pehle se URL hai.

pattern 2 (nirantar): design loading states

  • Ek route poore segment ke liye ek loading.tsx par rely kar sakta hai — aksar kaafi jabki page ek unit ke roop me load hota hai. Jaise tum data access ko neeche push karte ho, focused <Suspense> boundaries use karo aur loading states jaanboojhkar choose karo; loading.tsx ek outer fallback ke roop me reh sakta hai ya jab zaroorat na ho to hataya ja sakta hai.
  • Independent regions ko alag-alag reveal karo: jab har completed region ke predictable dimensions hon aur wo apne aap reveal ho sakta hai to sibling boundaries; har fallback ko apne completed region ki zaroorat wali space reserve karni chahiye.
  • Related regions ko steps me reveal karo: jab group ko pehli baar ek saath appear hona chahiye to zyada coarse-grained reveal, ya jab akele ek variable-height region ka reveal neeche ki content ko move kar sakta hai. React abhi bhi usi render ke dauraan independently reachable kaam start kar sakta hai — nesting reveal order badalti hai, request sequencing nahi. Variable-length content ke liye, dusra option ek predictable collapsed state hai jisme ek show more / load more control ho taaki content neeche ki cheezein move kiye bina appear ho.
  • Parallel route slots har ek apni loading state ke saath stream ho sakte hain.
  • Loading aur completed ke liye ek hi layout UI use karo: fallbacks completed UI se components/responsive layout changes ke roop me drift karte hain. Us container ko rakho jo boundary ke bahar layout ka owner hai — jaise skeleton card aur completed product card ek hi responsive <ProductGrid> ke andar; skeleton ko component ke paas rakho (ya usi file se export karo) taaki update/reuse aasan ho. Sirf ek empty fallback use karo jab resolved component ka koi visual footprint na ho (jaise ek auth gate jo null return karta hai); warna completed UI ke liye ek space-reserving fallback do.
  • Related data-fetching pattern: streamed regions me split karna requests ko zaroorat se baad me start hone se rokta hai — ek region me multiple independent requests ke liye parallel data fetching; ek data dependency ko jaldi start karna preload karke jab React use baad me render me reach karega.

pattern 3: cache pun: prayojy kaam

  • Blocking kaam ko alag karne ke baad, poochho ki kya result per-request recompute karna chahiye. Jab reusable ho, to function/component ko cache karo, isliye uski completed UI static shell me render hoti hai, freshness needs ke hisaab se lifetime ke saath:
tsx
// After: the reusable result can render in the shell
import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'

export async function ProductList() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')

  const products = await db.products.findMany()
  return <List products={products} />
}
  • Agar app cached result ko badal sakta hai, to cached reads ko on-demand revalidation ke saath unke writes se connect karo.
  • Related patterns: cookies()/headers()/kisi runtime API se ek value use karke ek result cache karne ke liye, value ko cached scope ke bahar padho aur use ek argument ke roop me pass karo; ek server request ke andar bina requests ke matching calls dedupe karne ke liye, React cache() use karo; known dynamic routes render karne aur baakiyon ko on demand generate karne ke liye, ISR with Cache Components dekho.

aap riphaiktar ke roop mein validation ka palan karein

  • Cache Components ke saath, next dev validate karta hai ki kya har page load ya client navigation ke paas instant UI hai. Ek route ke paas ek entry point ke liye instant UI ho sakta hai lekin dusre ke liye ek insight — jaise ek shared layout me ek fallback ek page load cover karta hai bina us layout ke andar ek client navigation cover kiye.
  • Ek insight ka matlab hai ki specific page load/client navigation ko instant result ya fallback chahiye — upar wale patterns ya optimizer skill ke liye ek useful target, bhale hi dusra access point pehle se instant ho. Card insights ko patterns se map karte hain: Cache ("use cache" component/data par) aur Stream (<Suspense> me wrapped).
  • Insight resolve karna us access point ko instant banata hai — ye decide nahi karta ki UI turant available hona chahiye. Zyada useful UI shamil karne ke liye patterns inspect karne ke liye Navigation Inspector use karo, ya optimizer skill ko route + desired instant UI do.

karya udaharan - team settings route (/[team]/setting)

  • Starting point (pre-Cache Components structure, aksar Pages Router getServerSideProps soch se carry over hua): layout ek-ek karke resolve karta hai (cookies() + headers() → getCurrentUser, agar koi nahi to settings frame render karne se pehle /login redirect); page heading render karne se pehle params + searchParams + team settings + plan details await karta hai. Koi settings UI static shell me nahi hai.
  • Step 1 — independent kaam ko URL ke peeche rakho: page turant <h1> return karta hai; ek outer <Suspense fallback={<SettingsContentSkeleton />}> SettingsTabs (Client Component) ko wrap karta hai aur ek nested <Suspense fallback={<SettingsFormSkeleton />}> TeamSettings ko wrap karta hai, jo settings query start karne se pehle dono URL values (Promise.all([params, searchParams])) await karta hai. Plan query URL values par depend nahi karti — use ek sibling PlanOptions component me move karo, isliye React use start karta hai jabki URL branch pending hai (ek temporary boundary ke saath). Result: heading seedhe render hoti hai; plan query aur URL-dependent branch independently start hoti hain. useSearchParams() Suspense
  • Step 2 — Suspense: reads ko cookies()/headers() ke peeche ek AuthGate me rakho; layout bina kisi await ke SettingsShell + children render karta hai. AuthGate request reads ka owner hai aur agar koi user nahi to redirect karta hai; ek empty fallback fit baithta hai kyunki ek authorized gate null bhi return karta hai. <Suspense fallback={null}>
  • Note: agar ek authorization intercept (unauthorized() / forbidden()) streaming start hone ke baad chalta hai, to ye apna UI render kar sakta hai lekin response ki status 200 rehti hai — agar 401/403 status matter karta hai, to streaming start hone se pehle access check karo. Ek layout redirect apne aap ek DB query ya Server Action ko protect nahi karta — data access functions me authorization check karo aur dusre ke complete hone se pehle shell me sirf safe UI shamil karo (Authentication with Cache Components dekho).
  • Step 3 — reusable plan data cache karo: team settings <Suspense> (current + authorized rehna chahiye) ke peeche request-time rehte hain, lekin plan details teams ke across shared hain aur ek known list par badalte hain — 'use cache' + cacheLife('hours') ko PlanOptions me jodo. Isme koi request-time dependency nahi hai, isliye Next.js static shell generate karte samay use resolve karta hai; uski boundary hatayi ja sakti hai (ek cached component pehle request-time data ke baad pahunchaya jata hai, jab ek cold cache cover hota hai). Agar plan details badalte hain to related mutation se on-demand revalidate karo.
  • Result teen steps me reveal hota hai: (1) static shell — heading + cached plan options, URL region apna fallback dikhata hai; (2) ek baar URL available ho — tabs content skeleton ko replace karte hain jabki settings query apne nested fallback ke peeche continue hoti hai; (3) settings load ke baad — poora form apne skeleton ki jagah leta hai.
  • Step 4 — instant UI verify karo: instant() test sirf heading + plan options + settings tabs + callback ke andar dikhai dene wale skeleton assert karta hai, aur content skeleton + poora form absent; callback ke baad, poora form dikhai deta hai aur uska skeleton gayab ho jata hai. Playwright assertions hydration ke baad chalte hain, isliye bina server content wale Client Components ko resolve karne yogya pehle se hi callback ke andar dikhai de sakte hain. Testing API next dev me automatic hai; next start ke saath ek production build ke liye, testing builds ke liye experimental.exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild enable karo. Poora route wahi settings data, redirects, error states aur interactions rakhe jo original me the.
  • Step 5 — instant UI me URL-specific content shamil karo: direct visit shared shell + SettingsContentSkeleton ke saath start hoti hai (root ko pehle searchParams nahi pata); ek baar URL available ho to tabs use replace karte hain. Ek client navigation ke dauraan SettingsTabs synchronously padhta hai; destination ke params/searchParams par based koi dusra server content shared shell ka hissa nahi hai — agar cacheable ho, to ek per-link prefetch click se pehle use resolve kar sakta hai (Optimizing prefetching dekho).

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Ek broad <Suspense> boundary (ya ek single loading.tsx) poore page ko replace karti hai — boundaries ko actually suspended regions tak neeche le jao.
  • Ek layout/page ke top par request data await karna — poore shell ko block karta hai.
  • Ek insight resolve karne ka matlab ye samajhna ki sahi UI shell me hai — validation sirf instant state check karta hai; Navigation Inspector se inspect karo.
  • Visual footprint wale components ke liye empty fallbacks — space reserve karo, warna layout shift hota hai.
  • Sequential requests expect karne wali boundaries — nesting sirf reveal order badalti hai.
  • Data access functions me auth checks bhool jana — akele ek layout queries/Server Actions ko protect nahi karta; aur streaming start hone ke baad auth intercepts status 200 chhod dete hain.

interview points

  • Teen patterns (static UI shell me rakho, request-time kaam stream karo, reusable kaam cache karo) aur har ek ko kaise apply karein.
  • Push-down techniques: data access ko ek Server Component me move karna, .then() ke saath ek Promise inline resolve karna, Client Components ko use() ke saath unwrap karne ke liye Promise pass karna.
  • Loading-state design: sibling vs nested boundaries, same layout skeletons, space reservation.
  • Settings-route worked example end-to-end (URL kaam → Suspense, auth → AuthGate, plan → 'use cache'), teen-step reveal aur instant() validation test.
Source — Asli Pagehttps://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
Hissa 68 / 471 · App Router · Guides

Optimizing package bundling

App RouterGuides

Ye page App Router (naya, recommended tareeka) ke Guides hisse ka hai, aur iska topic hai Optimizing package bundling. Neeche saare main points ek-ek karke diye hain — code examples bilkul docs jaise hi hain, taaki tumhe asli docs dobara kholne ki zaroorat na pade.

Asaan bhasha me samjho: Optimizing package bundling — ye topic Next.js me roz ke kaam ki cheez hai, aur is section ko padhne ke baad tumhe iske liye docs nahi kholne padenge. Isme khaas taur par ye baatein cover hongi: Bundling, Next.js Bundle Analyzer (Turbopack; v16.1+), Step 1 — run, Step 2 — filter/inspect, Step 3 — trace modules with import chains, Step 4 — write output to disk. Har baat ko neeche alag point me khol kar samjhaya gaya hai — pehle point se shuru karo aur ek-ek karke aage badho. Dhyaan rahe: ye App Router wala tareeka hai — Server Components yahan default hote hain, isliye jo baat yahan kahi gayi hai wo Pages Router par waisi ki waisi lagu nahi hogi.

Poori Detail — Saare Points Ek-Ek Karke

Main Points — Pehle Ye Samjho

  • Bundling = application code aur dependencies ko client aur server ke liye optimized output files me combine karna. Chhote bundles tez load hote hain, JS execution time kam karte hain, Core Web Vitals improve karte hain, aur server cold start times kam karte hain.
  • Next.js bundles ko automatically optimize karta hai (code splitting, tree-shaking, wagera), lekin kuch cases me manual optimization chahiye hoti hai.
  • Do analysis tools: Turbopack ke liye Next.js Bundle Analyzer aur Webpack ke liye @next/bundle-analyzer plugin.

Next.js bundle vishleshak (Turbopack; v16.1+)

  • Turbopack ke module graph ke saath integrated — badi dependencies khojne ke liye precise import tracing ke saath server aur client modules inspect karo. Feedback: GitHub discussion vercel/next.js #86731; demo: turbopack-bundle-analyzer-demo.vercel.sh.
  • Step 1 — run: npx next analyze (yarn/pnpm/bun equivalents) aur browser me interactive view kholo.
  • Step 2 — filter/inspect: route, environment (client/server), aur type (JavaScript, CSS, JSON) se filter karo, ya file se search karo.
  • Step 3 — import chain ke saath module trace karo: treemap har module ko uske size ke hisaab se area wale rectangle ke roop me dikhata hai; ek module par click karke uska size, uski puri import chain, aur exactly kahan use hota hai, dekho.
  • Step 4 — sharing/diffing ke liye output disk par likho: npx next analyze --output .next/diagnostics/analyze par likhta hai — compare karne ke liye kahin aur copy karo, jaise cp -r .next/diagnostics/analyze ./analyze-before-refactor
  • Analysis data export karo (v16.4+): next analyze export ek saved snapshot ko scripts/AI tools ke liye JSON Lines ke roop me stream karta hai, bina rebuild kiye ya server start kiye:
bash
npx next analyze --output --snapshot before
npx next analyze export --snapshot before > bundle-graph.jsonl

export vikalpon ke liye CLI sandarbh dekhein.

  • Apne AI agent ko access do: next-bundle-optimizer skill (skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-bundle-optimizer) ek agent ko analyzer data deta hai jo automatically un bade client-side bundles ke sources identify karta hai jo initial load ko hurt karte hain. npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer ke saath install karo, phir audit-only mode me prompt karo ("Is site ke initial load performance ki report banane ke liye next-bundle-optimizer skill use karo") ya issues fix karne / kisi specific route par focus karne ko kaho.

@next/bundle-analyzer for Webpack

  • Ek plugin jo har package ke size aur dependencies ki visual report generate karta hai — badi dependencies hatane, code split karne ya lazy-load karne ke liye ise use karo.
  • Step 1 — install: pnpm add @next/bundle-analyzer, phir config wrap karo:
js
// next.config.js
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {}

const withBundleAnalyzer = require('@next/bundle-analyzer')({
  enabled: process.env.ANALYZE === 'true',
})

module.exports = withBundleAnalyzer(nextConfig)
  • Step 2 — ek report generate karo: ANALYZE=true npm run build (yarn/pnpm equivalents) — report inspect karne ke liye teen naye browser tabs khulti hain.

bare bundles ka optimization karna

  • Kai exports wale packages (icon/utility libraries jo sainkadon modules export karti hain): next.config.js me experimental.optimizePackageImports use karo — sirf actually use hue modules load hote hain, jabki convenient named-import syntax bana rehta hai:
js
// next.config.js
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    optimizePackageImports: ['icon-library'],
  },
}

Next.js kuchh libraries ko automatic roop se customize karta hai - unhein list mein rahne ki requirement nahi hai ( optimizePackageImports sandarbh mein puri list dekhein).

  • Heavy client workloads: bade client bundles ka ek common kaaran Client Components me mehnga rendering kaam hai — libraries jo sirf UI ke liye data transform karti hain (syntax highlighting, chart rendering, markdown parsing). Agar kaam ko browser API ya user interaction nahi chahiye, to use Server Component me chalao. Example: ek Client Component me Prism-based highlighter poori highlighting library client ko ship karta hai, bhale hi output sirf ek <code> block ho. Iske bajaye, Server Component par highlight karo (jaise server par Shiki ka codeToHtml) aur client ko sirf rendered markup bhejo:
tsx
// app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx (Server Component)
import { codeToHtml } from 'shiki'

export default async function Page() {
  const code = `export function hello() {
    console.log("hi")
  }`

  // The Shiki package runs on the server and is never bundled for the client.
  const highlightedHtml = await codeToHtml(code, {
    lang: 'tsx',
    theme: 'github-dark',
  })

  return (
    <article>
      <h1>Blog Post Title</h1>
      <pre>
        <code dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: highlightedHtml }} />
      </pre>
    </article>
  )
}
  • Specific packages ko bundling se opt out karna: Server Components/Route Handlers me imported packages automatically Next.js dwara bundle hote hain. next.config.js me serverExternalPackages ke saath specific packages ko exclude karo:
js
const nextConfig = {
  serverExternalPackages: ['package-name'],
}

sanskaran history

  • v16.4.0 — next analyze export aur next-bundle-optimizer skill jodta hai.

Aam Galtiyaan — Dhyaan Do

  • Turbopack (default) use karte hue sirf Webpack plugin se bundles analyze karna — next analyze use karo.
  • Client Components me heavy transform libraries (highlighting, charts, markdown) rakhna — jab koi browser API/interaction nahi chahiye to Server Components ki taraf jao.
  • Poori icon/utility libraries ko optimizePackageImports (ya deep imports) ke bina import karna.

interview points

  • Chhote bundles kyun matter karte hain (load time, JS execution, Core Web Vitals, cold starts) aur Next.js automatically kya karta hai (code splitting, tree-shaking).
  • Do analyzers (next analyze Turbopack ke liye import chains ke saath treemap + JSONL export; ANALYZE=true ke saath Webpack ke liye @next/bundle-analyzer).
  • Teen fixes: kai-export packages ke liye optimizePackageImports, heavy kaam ko Server Components me le jana, bundling se opt out karne ke liye serverExternalPackages.
